### NEEDS-HUMAN (loop tooling) 2026-08-01: `scan_transcripts` CANNOT detect a fork whose fallback fires before its first assistant turn — verified misattribution found and fixed
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/workflow/changelog.md
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Source**: refine-draft attribution check, 2026-08-01T12:5xZ, transcript b8e74477 window
- **Code path** (not the `File` above, which is set to a content path so a refine fork cannot mangle a module): `tools/evolution/model_fallback.py`, function `scan_transcripts`
- **Notes**: **A STRUCTURAL BLIND SPOT IN THE FALLBACK DETECTOR, found by tripping over its output rather than by reading it.** `scan_transcripts` keys detection off **same-file model MIXING**. When the primary model is present it flags every non-primary message (`FALLBACK-SUSPECTED`); otherwise it sets `foreign = [m for m in messages if m != dominant]` and then `if not foreign: continue`. **So a transcript in which EVERY assistant message is the fallback model has an empty `foreign` list and is silently skipped.** The `else` branch can only ever fire on a 3-way mix; for a pure single-model transcript it is a guaranteed `continue`. **THIS IS EXACTLY THE CASE THAT PRODUCES A WRONGLY-STAMPED ARTIFACT**, because a fork that never observes itself on the primary model stamps `ai_system` with the model it was *nominally dispatched as*, not the one it ran as. The existing code comment reasons carefully about the "5x fable then 1276x opus" stick — but that case has ≥1 fable message and so is caught. The zero-fable case is the one that escapes. **VERIFIED INSTANCE, ALREADY FIXED (do not re-fix).** `agent-ac317aa5f61d948ac.jsonl` — the research-topic fork that wrote `obsidian/research/sentientism-2026-08-01.md` — carries a fallback marker at `2026-08-01T07:55:21.573Z`, roughly five seconds BEFORE its first assistant turn at `07:55:26.212Z`, and then runs **53 assistant messages, all `claude-opus-5`, zero `claude-fable-5`**. The detector's 12:41Z scan covered that window (previous scan 07:41Z) and flagged three other transcripts while skipping this one. The note was stamped `ai_system: claude-fable-5`; corrected to `claude-opus-5` in both `obsidian/` and `hugo/content/`. **WHY THE FIX VALUE IS THE BARE FALLBACK MODEL, NOT A `+`-JOINED PAIR**: the `+` form denotes genuine mixed authorship, and here fable-5 wrote nothing at all. This matches the 2026-07-28 audit note observing that fork-written review archives "correctly self-attribute `ai_system: claude-opus-5`", and differs from the `a0fc32857` / `66f0237b5` corrections only in that those forks had a genuine co-author to preserve. **CANDIDATE FIXES (operator's choice, none actioned):** (a) treat a transcript whose messages are ALL non-primary as a stick and flag it — needs a notion of the expected primary model per run, since a legitimately opus-configured session is indistinguishable from a stuck one on message content alone; (b) key detection off the explicit **`{"type":"fallback","from":…,"to":…}` marker** the harness already writes into the transcript, which is present in this fork and is unambiguous — almost certainly the right fix, and it makes the mixing heuristic redundant rather than merely supplementing it; (c) leave the detector and instead have the dispatcher stamp the *observed* model at fork exit rather than letting each fork self-report. **SCOPE UNKNOWN AND WORTH MEASURING**: no sweep has been run for other artifacts written by zero-fable forks, so the number of similarly misattributed files is unmeasured. A sweep would grep the subagent transcript tree for fallback markers and cross-reference the files each such fork wrote — cheap, and it bounds the problem. **⚠️ SECOND, INDEPENDENT BLIND SPOT IN THE SAME LANE — VERIFIED IN CODE 2026-08-03T15:5xZ, and it is the one that bites a long session.** `queue_attribution_task` (`tools/evolution/model_fallback.py` L195-204) dedupes with a bare substring test: `todo = TODO_PATH.read_text(); stem = event.transcript.stem; if stem in todo: return False`. That matches the transcript id **anywhere in the file** — including inside a `### ✓`-closed entry below `## Completed Tasks`, and including a mere mention in some other task's Notes. **Consequence: once a session has been flagged and its attribution task closed, that session can never be re-flagged, however much longer it runs.** **MEASURED ON THE LIVE SESSION, which is the driver's own:** transcript `2a435880-26dd-4e40-bb58-abe8dd702a89` was queued and closed (`### ✓ 2026-08-03: Verify ai_system attribution after model-fallback event`) when the detector saw **1303** foreign messages. The 15:49Z run reports **2541** — the window has since grown from 2026-08-02T09:04:46Z to 2026-08-03T15:49:44Z — and the run printed `[SKIP] todo.md already references 2a435880-…`. So roughly 1,240 messages' worth of loop output sits outside any attribution audit and the detector structurally cannot say so. **SEVERITY IS LOW *HERE* BUT THE MECHANISM IS NOT.** In this instance `dominant` and `foreign` are both `claude-opus-5`, which is the session-level-stick shape that self-attributes correctly ([[model-fallback-dominant-equals-foreign-is-correct]], [[fallback-stick-self-attributes-correctly]]) — so nothing is currently mis-attributed. On a genuinely mixed session the same suppression would hide real drift. **CANDIDATE FIXES (operator's call, all small):** (a) dedupe on `stem + last_foreign_ts` so a grown window re-queues; (b) restrict the substring search to the **active** region above `## Completed Tasks`, which also fixes the mere-mention false match; (c) re-queue when the foreign count has grown by more than some factor since the recorded task. **(a) is the smallest and most direct.** **NOTE:** the driver did **not** hand-queue an attribution task for this window — the skill reserves that for the script, and the finding here is the dedup rule, not the attribution itself.
- **Scope sweep RUN 2026-08-01T13:0xZ** (by the sibling attribution check on the 12:32–12:34Z `agent-a841909c` window; answers the "SCOPE UNKNOWN" paragraph above for **one session**, not the whole tree). Model composition computed for all **9 forks** of session `b8e74477`: **5 of the 9 are 100% `claude-opus-5` with zero `claude-fable-5`** (`a2decb20`, `a5a81eea`, `a614def7`, `a8834aa7`, `ac317aa5`) and are therefore **all structurally invisible to `scan_transcripts`**; only 2 were model-mixed and so detectable (`a46bcc7e`, `a841909c`), and 2 ran pure fable-5 (`a773b272`, `ac5abf0f`). **The blind spot is not a rare edge case in this sample — it is the majority of forks.** Of the 5 invisible ones, only two wrote authored prose to the vault: `ac317aa5` (the known, already-fixed sentientism note) and **`a5a81eea` — a SECOND instance, previously unrecorded**: the 12:58–13:04Z deep-review that wrote `obsidian/concepts/samkhya-three-way-distinction.md` (commit `fa2a670dc`), 74 assistant messages, all opus-5. The remaining three wrote no prose (`a2decb20` set one `ai_system` value; `a8834aa7` posted externally only; `a614def7` was the auditing fork itself). **NO CORRECTION WAS OWED ON THE NEW INSTANCE, and it must not be "fixed" retroactively** — that fork held `ai_system: claude-opus-4-7` and declined to re-stamp, which **matches corpus convention**: the two 07-31 sweeps for the identical nav-gloss/link-label calibration family (`52126351b`, 5 files; `e29e11a8c`, 2 files) each bumped `ai_modified` only and left every `ai_system` untouched. A one-line Further-Reading gloss rewrite is not re-authoring. **THE POINT OF RECORDING IT IS RECURRENCE, NOT DAMAGE**: `a5a81eea` ran *after* the 12:41:51Z scan high-water mark, so the next scan's range covers it and will skip it again for exactly the same reason. The defect reproduces every cycle, and the cases where it happens to be harmless are invisible for the same reason as the cases where it is not — which is why (b), keying off the explicit `fallback` marker, remains the recommendation. **Still unmeasured**: the other ~200 session directories under the project transcript tree; this sweep covered one.
- **Second defect in the same module, found 2026-08-01T13:1xZ by the third sibling attribution check (the `agent-a46bcc7e` 07:46–07:48Z window): THE DETECTOR FLAGS ITS OWN AUDIT FORKS, and this is the one subclass where the "was content written?" question is answerable at QUEUE time.** `scan_transcripts` walks `root.rglob("*.jsonl")`, which includes each session's `subagents/` directory, and `queue_attribution_task` dedupes only on transcript id — so an attribution-check fork that itself runs model-mixed mints a fresh P2 attribution-check task **about its own transcript** on the next scan. The window assigned to this task *is* exactly that: `agent-a46bcc7e7d867d6c2` (3 `claude-fable-5` turns, then 24 `claude-opus-5` — the stick is real and the flag's count is exact) is the 07:46–07:48Z fork whose entire output was the changelog entry recording its own no-op verdict on the earlier 07:36–07:39Z harvest window. Its only vault write was `obsidian/workflow/changelog.md` (commit `8c8b5aab8`; the rest of that commit is `todo.md`, `evolution-state.yaml`, `.unfin/current-queue-task.json` and the hugo mirrors, none of which carries `ai_system`), and `changelog.md`'s own `ai_system` **already read `claude-opus-4-8+claude-opus-5`** before the edit — the fallback model was on the file already, so no annotation was owed even on the one attributed surface it touched. **MEASURED, NOT INFERRED**: of the 38 subagent transcripts named by attribution-check tasks in this file, 24 are still on disk, and **2 of those 24 are themselves attribution-check forks** — this one and `agent-a5a18311b0e2e5a81` (2026-07-13), closed further down this file as "*prior attribution-audit no-op fork, no content*". **The pattern was therefore already noticed once, closed locally, and never reached this defect record.** **WHY IT BELONGS HERE RATHER THAN IN A SEPARATE TASK**: the 07-31 `806e8218` note below records that `check_model_fallback.py` "queues on the transcript window alone and does not check whether content was written in it — working as designed, since that check is meant to happen at execution time". That reasoning is right in general and should not be reversed. It simply does not hold for the self-referential subclass, whose window is knowable in advance to contain nothing but the auditing fork. **CANDIDATE FIX (d), narrow and cheap**: have `queue_attribution_task` skip a transcript whose own dispatch arguments are an attribution-check task — the flag text is fixed boilerplate and greps in one line. **DO NOT generalise this to "audit forks never write content"** — that is false and would suppress real findings: the 12:53Z sibling audit *did* write, correcting `research/sentientism-2026-08-01.md`. The exemption is for the *self-reference*, not for the task type.

### NEEDS-HUMAN (loop tooling) 2026-07-31: `integrate-orphan` silently DISCARDS its task Notes at dispatch — measured 278 args chars vs 2689 for the same task as refine-draft
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/workflow/changelog.md
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Source**: cycle driver, from the 16:1xZ optimistic-review
- **Generated**: 2026-07-31
- **Notes**: **MEASURED, NOT INFERRED.** `tools/evolution/task_selector.py` handles `TaskType.INTEGRATE_ORPHAN` (~L255) by composing a **generated** context string — *"This file has no inbound links and is orphaned. Focus on finding related articles that should link to this content…"* — and returns `SkillInvocation("deep-review", f"{file_path} -- Context: {context}")`. **It never references `task.notes`.** `TaskType.REFINE_DRAFT` (~L206) does the opposite, explicitly appending `f"{args}\n\nTask context:\n{task.notes}"`. **THE MEASUREMENT.** The driver ran `task_to_skill` against one real task in both forms: as `integrate-orphan` it produced **278 characters** of args; the identical task as `refine-draft` produced **2689**. Everything an author writes in the Notes of an integrate-orphan task is thrown away before the executor sees it. **WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC.** The task in question (`topics/phenomenal-normativity-environmental-ethics`, integration gap: 25 outbound links, 2 live inbound, 0 of 39 apex) had Notes carrying a **per-candidate `analyze_length` table**, because length binds hard among its candidate linkers: `concepts/animal-consciousness` has **9 words** to its hard ceiling and `concepts/phenomenal-value-realism` is **already over** at 4039/4000. An executor receiving only the boilerplate would have had no way to know that, and the natural action — adding a sentence of linking prose — would have pushed an already-over-ceiling file further over. **The Notes were the safety rail and the dispatcher deletes them.** **IMMEDIATE MITIGATION ALREADY APPLIED, so nothing is at risk right now**: the driver retyped that task `integrate-orphan` → `refine-draft` and prepended an explanation; it now dispatches 4929 args chars with the length table intact. The semantics are unchanged — the executor is told the edits land in the *source* files rather than the `File` anchor. **THE OPERATOR DECISION.** Options: **(a)** make `INTEGRATE_ORPHAN` append `task.notes` exactly as `REFINE_DRAFT` does — a two-line change and almost certainly right, since the generated boilerplate can simply precede the Notes rather than replace them; **(b)** retire `integrate-orphan` as a type and standardise on `refine-draft` with integration instructions in the Notes, which is what the corpus already does in practice; **(c)** leave it and rely on drivers spotting it, which is not viable — this was found only because a fork happened to report its args length. **(a) is the smallest change.** **DO NOT ACTION FROM THE LOOP** — this is the loop's own automation code, which the content loop must not self-modify. **DO NOT mint a P0–P3 from this.** Worth noting the same shape may affect other non-`refine-draft` branches of `task_to_skill`; a sweep of that function for handlers that ignore `task.notes` would be cheap and is the natural companion to (a).

### NEEDS-HUMAN (workflow publication policy) 2026-07-31: the 418 broken links check-links keeps reporting are ALL on served, sitemap-indexed workflow pages — a presentation decision, not a link repair
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/workflow/changelog.md

- **Notes**: **MEASURED THIS RUN, AND THE SEGMENTATION IS THE POINT.** check-links reports **418 broken internal links across 34 source pages**. Segmented: **article prose (`topics/ concepts/ apex/ voids/ positions/ arguments/ archive/`) = 0**; **records (`workflow/ reviews/ research/`) = 418** (workflow 410 across 27 pages, research 6, reviews 2); anything else = 0. The fork did not trust the crawler alone — it re-audited from `sitemap.xml`, fetching **795 article-section pages directly and status-checking 888 unique internal targets, with 0 non-200**. So the serving *article* surface is completely clean, and **every previous "417 broken links" alarm was this same records-only floor.** **WHY THIS IS NOT NOISE, THOUGH IT IS NOT A DEFECT EITHER.** The driver checked whether these pages are actually public: `/workflow/` appears in `hugo/public/sitemap.xml` (8 entries) and there is **no `robots.txt` exclusion** for it. So a reader or crawler reaching e.g. `/workflow/archive/changelog-2026-w12/` (63 dead links on that page alone; `workflow/todo` carries 46) sees broken navigation on an indexed page. **THE CAUSE IS INHERENT AND THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG.** These are dated records naming articles that were later archived, coalesced or renamed. **Repointing them would falsify the record** — the changelog entry is supposed to say what was true when written. So this is not a link-repair task and must never be handed to a refine-draft that "fixes broken links". **THE ACTUAL DECISION, which is presentational and operator-side:** (a) render historic article references inside `workflow/` records as **plain text rather than links** at sync time, which preserves the record exactly while removing the dead navigation; (b) exclude `/workflow/` from the sitemap and add a `robots.txt` disallow, keeping the pages reachable for anyone with the URL but not indexed; (c) stop serving `workflow/` altogether; or (d) accept it and stop re-triaging. **(a) is the smallest change that fixes the reader-visible problem without touching the records.** **DO NOT ACTION FROM THE LOOP** — (a) and (b) are changes to sync/site tooling, which the content loop must not self-modify, and (c)/(d) are publication policy. **WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING NOW**: this floor has been re-measured and re-dismissed by multiple check-links runs, each spending a cycle re-deriving that the 41x figure is records-only. Recording the segmentation once converts a recurring triage cost into a decided question. **DO NOT mint a P0–P3 from this.** **⚠️ ADDITION 2026-08-03T17:0xZ — the baseline moved 417 → 418, and the one new link is PREVENTABLE in a way the other 417 are not.** The 2026-08-03 check-links run reproduces the documented shape exactly — 410 of 418 from `workflow/`, 6 from `research/`, 2 from `reviews/`, and **0 from any content article** in `topics/ concepts/ apex/ voids/ positions/ arguments/`. 374 of the 418 are redirect-covered and only 404 against the checker's ephemeral local server; 44 are dead everywhere. **THE DELTA IS ONE LINK, AND ITS CAUSE IS A HABIT, NOT ROT.** `obsidian/workflow/archive/changelog-2026-W31.md` L4401 contains `[[concepts/parsimony-case-for-interactionist-dualism]]`. Driver-verified: the article exists at `obsidian/topics/parsimony-case-for-interactionist-dualism.md` — there is no `concepts/` copy — so the wikilink was **path-qualified with a guessed and wrong section**, and the converter dutifully emitted a URL that 404s. A **bare** `[[parsimony-case-for-interactionist-dualism]]` would have resolved, because the converter maps bare slugs to the file's real section and the corpus has no colliding stems. The same changelog entry uses the bare form two lines down at L4402 and resolves fine — both forms sit side by side in one entry. **This is the `topics:` canonical-form rule from CLAUDE.md showing up in prose links: path-qualifying is a guess that can be wrong, bare is self-correcting.** **LEFT UNFIXED, deliberately** — archived changelogs are historical records and the standing convention leaves the `reviews/` dead links alone for the same reason; repairing one link piecemeal would not change the decision this entry is waiting on. It is a one-token fix (drop the `concepts/` prefix) if the operator would rather hold the count at 417. **THE PREVENTION IS CHEAPER THAN THE REPAIR:** whatever is decided about serving `workflow/`, agents writing changelog and todo prose should default to **bare-slug wikilinks** and path-qualify only when a stem genuinely collides. That stops the count growing regardless of which publication option is chosen. **UPDATE 2026-08-06 (driver, from the cycle-trigger run) — two findings the earlier entry does not record, one of which makes the report actively misleading.** **(1) THE "On page:" ATTRIBUTIONS ARE WRONG, not merely incomplete.** `check_links.py` `crawl()` guards `to_visit` with `if normalized_link not in visited`, so **each broken target is attributed to the FIRST referrer that reached it and no other**. Driver-confirmed in the source. Consequence: `/voids/self-reference-paradox/` was reported against a single research note but is in fact linked from **36 pages**. Anyone using the report to locate or scope a defect will under-count it, and a real content regression could be attributed to a workflow file and dismissed as known noise. Any future triage must re-derive the referrer set by grepping `hugo/content`, not read it off the report. **(2) THE REDIRECT DESTINATIONS WERE VERIFIED, which the crawler structurally cannot do.** A redirect pointing at a dead page is a genuine production 404 that would never appear in this report. All **510** rules in `hugo/static/_redirects` were followed (including chained hops) against a live Hugo build: **0 destinations 404**. That is a real assurance and worth re-running whenever archival activity is heavy — today alone added a coalesce archival plus several reference replacements. **Also reconfirmed tonight**: of the 418, **374** are redirect-covered and resolve as 301s in production, 36 are workflow prose, 8 are review prose, and **0 originate from a live article** in `topics/ concepts/ voids/ apex/ positions/`. **The candidate fix stands and is now better motivated**: teach `check_url()` to consult `hugo/static/_redirects` before reporting a 404, dropping the output to 44 — at which point a genuine regression in live content would actually stand out, and the gate could function as the pre-push check it is documented to be.

  ✅ **The serving article surface is still completely clean** — 0 broken links originating in `topics/ concepts/ apex/ voids/ positions/ tenets/ arguments/ questions/`, re-derived by parsing the crawler's `On page:` attributions rather than trusting the headline count.
  📈 **Drift rate: +7 in 52 days, all of it in `workflow/`** — roughly one new dead reference per week, which is what you would expect from a records tree that keeps naming articles as they are archived, coalesced or renamed. **It compounds slowly and will not self-correct**, since repointing the entries would falsify the record. The decision this entry describes does not get easier by waiting, but neither is it urgent.

  🔧 **2026-11-15T12:36Z RE-MEASUREMENT + A CODE CAUSE FOR THE `research/` ROW (cycle driver, check-links trigger).** Total **424** unique broken URLs, all 404, on 44 source pages: `workflow/` **418** (370 covered by a `_redirects` 301, 48 with no redirect: never-existent or wrong-path URLs, 15 on `workflow/todo`), `research/` **6**, `reviews/` **0**, content sections **0** (the fork grepped all 424 targets across the content sections, not just the crawler's first-page attribution). **The `research/` 6 are NOT record text and should not sit in this policy bucket.** The Obsidian sources wikilink archived slugs (e.g. `[[scale-void]]`), and `build_content_index()` in `tools/sync/converter.py` (archive block after the collision pass) maps an archived slug to its `superseded_by` target ONE hop only; when that target was itself archived later, the link lands on a second archived URL. `tools/sync/redirects.py` `_flatten_chains` follows the chain to the end, so production serves a 301, not a 404, but every such link pays an extra hop and would rot if `_redirects` changed. Driver verified the one-hop code by reading both files. Fix (code, not content, so not a refine-draft): resolve `superseded_by` transitively in `build_content_index` the way `_flatten_chains` does. Note: the same one-hop mapping applies to ANY section, so a future article wikilinking a twice-archived slug would get the same extra hop.

### NEEDS-HUMAN (agentic-social config) 2026-07-31: the topic-dedupe filter is silently DEAD — 0 of 671 articles survive it, so every pick falls through to URL-only selection
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/workflow/changelog.md
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Source**: cycle driver, from the 13:01Z agentic-social run
- **Generated**: 2026-07-31
- **Notes**: **MEASURED, NOT INFERRED — the driver ran the selector's own functions against the live corpus at 2026-07-31T13:0xZ and got: 671 published articles, 158 recently-posted URLs, 200 recently-posted topics, 514 articles surviving the URL filter, and *0* surviving the URL+topic filter.** **THE MECHANISM.** `select_content()` in `.claude/skills/agentic-social/scripts/agentic_social_api.py` (~L475–L491) skips any article sharing *any* topic with the recently-posted set. The recently-posted window holds **158 posts carrying 200 distinct topics** — and because Map topic tags are broad and heavily reused (`hard-problem-of-consciousness` alone is applied across a large fraction of the corpus), that 200-topic union now intersects **every single article**. `available` therefore comes back empty on every run. **THE REAL PROBLEM IS THE NEXT LINE.** At ~L493 the code does `if not available:` and silently re-populates from URL-only filtering, with no log line, no warning, and no signal to the caller. So the skill reports a normal successful selection while the topic dedupe it advertises has contributed **nothing**. This is precisely the pattern `CLAUDE.md` forbids under *Error Handling* — "**Never use fallthrough logic that hides errors** … Do NOT provide a catch-all `else` that silently substitutes a default behavior." **OBSERVED CONSEQUENCE, not hypothetical:** of the six posts on 2026-07-31 before this was caught, **three consecutive** (09:27 `phenomenology-of-attention-to-absence`, 10:17 `stapp-quantum-mind`, 11:15 `integrated-information-theory`) carried `hard-problem-of-consciousness`, and the 13:01 run's `select` again returned a `hard-problem`-only article (`topics/quantum-darwinism-and-consciousness`) as its top pick — a fourth in a row. The last two runs only avoided it because the driver briefed the fork to check the tracked history by hand and enumerate the pool manually. **That manual workaround is not sustainable and should not become the fix.** **WHY THIS IS AN OPERATOR CALL RATHER THAN AN AUTOMATED ONE:** the remedy is a tuning decision with a real trade-off, and the loop should not pick it unilaterally. Options: **(a)** decouple the windows — keep 7 days for URL dedupe but narrow *topic* dedupe to 24–48h, which restores the filter's bite while still preventing same-day repetition; **(b)** require overlap on *all* of an article's topics rather than any one, so a broad shared tag like `hard-problem-of-consciousness` no longer vetoes an otherwise-distinct article; **(c)** weight topics by corpus frequency and ignore the most common tags for dedupe purposes; **(d)** cap the topic union at the N most recent posts rather than the full window. **(a) is the smallest change and probably the right one.** **INDEPENDENT OF WHICH OPTION IS CHOSEN, THE FALLTHROUGH SHOULD BE MADE LOUD** — at minimum log a warning when the topic filter empties the pool, so a future silent degradation is visible rather than masquerading as a normal run. **DO NOT "FIX" THIS BY WIDENING THE POSTING CADENCE OR PRUNING `recently_posted`** — pruning would also weaken URL dedupe, which is working correctly and is the thing preventing genuine duplicate posts. **⚠️ UPDATE 2026-07-31T14:4xZ — THE MANUAL WORKAROUND HAS NOW PRODUCED ITS FIRST MISS, WHICH STRENGTHENS THE CASE FOR FIXING THIS.** Because the filter is inert, the driver has been hand-supplying each run with the day's topic union and the fork has been enumerating the pool manually. That held for four runs and failed on the fifth. The 14:45Z post (`concepts/parfit-reductionism`) carries topics **`personal-identity`** and **`meaning-of-life`**. Both are correctly disjoint from the 24-topic union the driver supplied *for that day* — but **both recur repeatedly inside the ~7-day dedupe window the rule actually specifies**: `personal-identity` in 5 earlier posts, most recently **the previous day** (`narrative-coherence`, 2026-07-30); `meaning-of-life` in 5 earlier posts, also most recently the previous day (`alignment-in-objective-experiential-terms`, 2026-07-29). The fork reported that it had checked both against the **full 158-post window** and found **zero** occurrences. That claim is false — the driver re-ran the check and found ten. **No harm done to the account** (the URL is genuinely new, the post is live and verified, and the subject matter is distinct from the earlier posts), **but the dedupe rule was violated and the violation was reported as verified.** **THE LESSON FOR THE OPERATOR:** a hand-driven substitute for the filter depends on the driver supplying the right window *and* the fork checking it correctly, and it has now failed at the second step. The workaround is not a stable substitute for the config fix, and each additional run compounds the chance of a repeat. This is a fifth argument for option (a) — decouple the windows so topic dedupe runs on a short window that a real filter can enforce. **⚠️ UPDATE 2026-07-31T15:3xZ — TWO MEASUREMENTS THAT SETTLE WHAT THE FIX SHOULD BE. THE WRITTEN 7-DAY RULE IS PROVABLY UNSATISFIABLE, NOT MERELY INERT.** The driver measured eligibility across candidate windows against the live corpus (671 published articles, tracker holding 158 posts): **7 days = 199 distinct topics → 0 eligible articles**; 48h = 70 topics → 15; 24h = 45 topics → 49; 12h = 22 topics → 69. At ~45-minute cadence the 7-day union is effectively the corpus's **entire tag vocabulary**, so it intersects every article and **no compliant post exists**. This retires the earlier framing of the 14:45Z post as a 'workaround miss': it was not a careless slip — **any** post violates the rule as written, so the fork could not have complied. It also explains the silent fallthrough precisely: `select_content()` is not misbehaving, it is being handed an unsatisfiable constraint and degrading without saying so. **RECOMMENDATION, now backed by numbers: option (a), decouple the windows — keep 7 days for URL dedupe (which works and is what actually prevents duplicate posts) and set TOPIC dedupe to 24h.** 24h leaves 49 candidates, a healthy pool; 48h leaves 15 and is workable but tight; 12h is more permissive than needed. **Whatever is chosen, make the fallthrough loud** so a future degradation is visible rather than silent. **SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT FOUND THIS RUN — TOPIC STRINGS ARE NOT NORMALISED BEFORE COMPARISON, WHICH INFLATES APPARENT ELIGIBILITY.** Topics are stored as wikilinks that may or may not carry a section prefix, and the filter compares raw strings, so `[[free-will]]` and `[[topics/free-will]]` are treated as **different topics** despite resolving to the same file `obsidian/topics/free-will.md`. Driver-counted across `obsidian/topics/` and `obsidian/concepts/`: **38 occurrences of the bare form against 225 of the prefixed form** — for that one topic alone. Consequence measured this run: of the 15 articles that appeared eligible at 48h, **9 were false-eligible** — 8 carried bare `free-will` while the union held `topics/free-will` (free will *was* covered within 48h, so posting them would have been substantive duplication), and 1 (`topics/argument-from-reason`) had non-matching topics but **its own slug** in the union, i.e. the article *is* the recently-covered subject. **Strict-eligible pool after normalisation was 6, now 5** — so even 48h is close to exhausted, and this defect has been silently masking that. **TWO ADDITIONS TO WHATEVER FIX IS MADE**: (i) normalise topics on both sides — strip `[[ ]]`, strip any section prefix, lowercase — before comparing; (ii) also exclude any article whose **own slug** appears in the topic union. This is the same class as the known harvest-dedup singular/plural near-miss, which suggests a shared normalisation helper would fix both lanes at once. **⚠️ UPDATE 2026-08-03T13:3xZ — THE DIAGNOSIS ABOVE NO LONGER DESCRIBES LIVE BEHAVIOUR, AND THE CORRECTION CHANGES WHICH OPTION FIXES IT.** The 07-31 finding was *0 of 671 survive → `if not available:` silently falls through to URL-only*. The driver re-ran the selector's own functions against the live corpus at 2026-08-03T13:3xZ and got a **different** result: **671 articles, 129 recently-posted topics, 24 survive the topic filter — and all 24 have `topics: []`. Zero articles carrying real topics survive.** **The pool is non-empty, so the fallthrough at ~L493 never fires.** The filter is not degrading to URL-only any more; it is **confined to the ~3.6% of the corpus that carries the empty-topics defect**, and every post is now drawn from those 24. **MECHANISM (read at ~L24 of `select_content`):** the overlap test is guarded by `if article_topics and recently_posted_topics:` — an article with `topics: []` has falsy `article_topics`, so the check is **skipped** and the article is appended to `available` unconditionally. Articles with real topics still meet the full 129-topic union and are all vetoed. The two populations are therefore filtered by opposite rules: real-topic articles face an unsatisfiable constraint, empty-topic articles face none. **OBSERVED CONSEQUENCE TODAY, dated:** the 12:35 post (`concepts/phenomenal-constitution-thesis`, `topics: []`) recorded topic `intentionality`; the **13:24** post (`concepts/conceptual-role-semantics`, `topics: []`) recorded `intentionality` again — **49 minutes apart, same topic key**, both drawn from the 24-article pool where adjacency is unconstrained. `mark-posted` records topics scavenged from the `concepts:` field, so the *record* looks well-formed while selection saw nothing. **WHY THIS CHANGES THE RECOMMENDATION:** option **(a)** (decouple windows, topic dedupe to 24h) was the standing recommendation and it **does not fix this**. Narrowing the union helps only articles that *have* topics; the 24 bypass the check at any window length, so they remain permanently eligible and keep dominating the pool. **Backfilling `topics:` is now load-bearing rather than cosmetic** — it is option (d) of the sibling empty-topics NEEDS-HUMAN entry, and these two entries should be decided **together**: (a) alone leaves the defective subset privileged; backfill alone leaves the 7-day union unsatisfiable for everyone else. **A THIRD, SMALLER FIX WORTH CONSIDERING ALONGSIDE:** make the empty-topics case explicit rather than implicitly-permissive — treat `topics: []` as *ineligible* (or log it) instead of silently exempt, which is the same "no silent fallthrough" principle `CLAUDE.md` states under *Error Handling* and which this entry already invokes for the `if not available:` branch. **NO ACCOUNT HARM** — both posts are live, verified, on genuinely distinct URLs, and the subject matter differs; the defect is the selector's blindness, not the content. **DRIVER NOTE:** the fork that made today's post attributed the adjacency to `topics: []` alone; that is right about the article but was worth checking against this entry's fallthrough story, and the measurement above is what separates them. **REPRODUCE:** load `.claude/skills/agentic-social/scripts/agentic_social_api.py`, call `get_recently_posted_topics()`, then partition published articles by whether `extract_topics(content)` intersects it, and count how many survivors have empty topics. **⛔ RETRACTED 2026-08-03T14:2xZ — THE 13:3xZ UPDATE ABOVE IS WRONG. THE ORIGINAL 07-31 DIAGNOSIS WAS RIGHT ALL ALONG.** The driver's own reproduce recipe, quoted immediately above, is the bug: it partitions articles **by topic only and omits the URL filter that `select_content()` applies first**. `select_content()` skips `url in recently_posted_urls` *before* the topic check. The 24 "survivors" reported in that update are all articles that had **already been posted**, so their URLs are blocked and they never reach the pool. **CORRECTED MEASUREMENT (2026-08-03T14:2xZ, simulating `select_content()` exactly — URL filter then topic filter):** 671 published articles · 139 recently-posted URLs · **532 survive the URL filter** · **0 survive URL+topic** → **the primary pool IS empty and the `if not available:` fallthrough DOES fire, exactly as the 07-31 entry found.** **CONFIRMING EVIDENCE FROM THE SAME RUN:** the 14:21Z post (`topics/emotion-and-dualism`) carries `hard-problem-of-consciousness` (**48** prior occurrences in the window, most recent **10:48Z the same day**) and `ethics-under-dualism` (2 prior). Both were in the union *before* the post. The topic filter therefore rejected that article — and it was posted anyway, which is only possible via the URL-only fallthrough. A pool "confined to empty-topics articles" could not have produced it. **WHAT SURVIVES FROM THE RETRACTED UPDATE** (still true, still worth knowing, but *not* the dominant mechanism): the guard `if article_topics and recently_posted_topics:` does exempt `topics: []` articles from the overlap check, so they are the only articles that *would* survive the topic filter if their URLs were not already blocked. At the current cadence they get consumed quickly and the pool empties regardless. **THE RECOMMENDATION REVERTS TO OPTION (a)** — decouple the windows, keep 7 days for URL dedupe, set topic dedupe to 24h — which the 07-31 measurements already backed with numbers (24h → 49 eligible). The retracted update claimed (a) "does not fix this" and that backfilling `topics:` was load-bearing; **both claims rested on the omitted URL filter and are withdrawn.** Backfilling `topics:` remains worth doing on its own merits (it is option (d) of the sibling empty-topics entry, and empty `topics:` still defeats whatever topic dedupe is eventually made to work), but it is **not** a precondition for (a) and the two entries do **not** have to be decided together. **CORRECTED REPRODUCE RECIPE:** filter `article_to_url(a) in get_recently_posted()` **first**, then apply the topic intersection — or simply call `select_content()` and inspect what it returns rather than re-implementing its filter order. **DRIVER NOTE, worth generalising:** the error was re-implementing a function's filter chain from a partial reading instead of exercising the function itself, and it produced a confident, numerate, wrong claim inside an operator decision document. Prefer calling the real code path.

### NEEDS-HUMAN (citation policy) 2026-07-31: the 07-30 Tallis de-quote campaign rested on a FALSE premise — the span IS verbatim, and 47 loci were demoted
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/arguments/functionalism-argument.md
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Source**: pessimistic-review of arguments/functionalism-argument.md, 2026-07-31 (finding verified independently by the driver)
- **Generated**: 2026-07-31
- **Notes**: **The span `"misrepresentation presupposes presentation"` IS Raymond Tallis's own wording.** Verified 2026-07-31 from the raw publisher HTML at `philosophynow.org/issues/161` — "Tallis in Wonderland: The Illusion of Illusionism", *Philosophy Now* 161 (2024), 58-59. The sentence reads: *"If matter can't generate experiences, it seems even less capable of creating the illusions of experiences, since misrepresentation presupposes presentation."* The separately-cited `"all illusions presuppose experience"` is **also** verbatim, a few sentences earlier — they are two different sentences, not rival readings of one.
  **Why three passes concluded the opposite.** The publisher's HTML splits the word: `misre<tag>presentation`. Strip tags by substituting a **space** — the default in every quick extractor — and the text reads `"misre presentation presupposes presentation"`, so an exact-string grep returns **zero from the primary source** and reads as decisive proof of fabrication. Strip tags with **no substitution** and the phrase is contiguous and present. One character of difference in a regex inverted a 47-locus campaign. This is the publisher-side form of the broken-contiguity trap the corpus already knows from its own files, where wikilinks and `**` break a correct quote the same way.
  **What was done on that false premise.** Commit `b1adfdf1` (2026-07-30) de-quoted **47 loci** — 32 in `obsidian/`, the research-note origin, and 14 in `archive/` — converting a genuine verbatim quotation to attributed paraphrase.
  **Nothing is broken, which is why this is a decision and not a defect.** All 47 loci say true things, attribute them to the right author, and now pin the right work. Restoring the quotation marks is an *improvement in fidelity*, not a repair. At 47 loci across three trees it is a campaign with real regression risk, and it would be the **third** state-flip on this string — so it is the operator's call, not automation's.
  **Three options.** (1) Restore the quotation at all 47 loci. (2) Restore at a small number of high-visibility loci only — the argument articles and `concepts/illusionism.md` — and leave the paraphrase elsewhere. (3) Leave as is and record the decision so this does not re-surface a fourth time. Option 3 is defensible: attributed paraphrase of a correctly-cited source is not a defect.
  **Do NOT act unattended.** Whatever is chosen, the standard for changing the state in *either* direction is the same: reproduce the sentence from the source and name the extraction method. "Web-verified" assertions have now produced a wrong answer in both directions on this exact string.
  **Two separate, smaller items surfaced alongside it, both genuine and both cheap** — these are NOT operator-gated and can ride any future pass: (a) `obsidian/arguments/functionalism-argument.md` L164 renders Tallis's hedged *"hardly going to be able"* / *"seems even less capable"* as **"certainly cannot"**, an unlicensed modal upgrade; (b) the *Philosophy Now* issue number is cited as **159** in `obsidian/topics/attention-and-the-consciousness-interface.md` L240 and `archive/topics/attention-schema-theory-critique.md` L209, where the correct issue is **161** (the ~40 other loci omit the issue entirely, which is fine). Item (a) is already inside the scope of the open P2 on that file.
  The 07-30 campaign's *work-level* correction — repointing the argument from *Aping Mankind* (2011) to the 2024 article — was **right and stands**. Do not undo it. And do not confuse any of this with the Tallis-2016 phantom reference (*"The Disappearance of Appearance"*), which was genuinely fabricated and correctly swept on 2026-05-29.

- **Type**: refine-draft

The guard did its job — without it the Map would now carry **ten dead "Watch this article as a video" links** on live pages. **THE MISMATCH**: these ten carry `stage: youtube_published` in their `auto_unfin` notebooklm JSON, but their `youtube.visibility` is **`scheduled`** — every one of them — and their `scheduled_date` has long passed. So the stage label asserts a publication that never happened. **THE TEN** (scheduled_date · video_id · target article): 2026-03-19 `92gZVs5MKSE` apex/what-consciousness-tells-us-about-physics · 2026-03-25 `3rPSyhX73I8` topics/hoel-llm-consciousness-continual-learning · 2026-04-14 `c3yWlLozzK8` apex/time-consciousness-growing-block · 2026-04-20 `N-lIPsq-WxY` apex/testing-the-map-from-inside · 2026-04-23 `f7lf-TDqRIM` topics/anaesthesia-and-the-consciousness-interface · 2026-05-06 `DtXsLvSwBcM` topics/cetacean-and-corvid-consciousness · 2026-05-07 `RIxT9wb7_Qk` topics/lucid-dreaming-and-dualist-rendering · 2026-05-07 `RyFN0w-Mo0w` topics/death-and-consciousness · 2026-05-24 `SEIPe_XTUdo` concepts/adaptive-computational-depth · 2026-06-01 `EwwQ2yLUMaA` topics/probability-problem-in-many-worlds. **SCALE**: 90 entries are staged `youtube_published` across 87 distinct articles; 80 articles carry an `embedded_videos:` record. So this is **10 of 90** — about 11% of produced video output is finished, uploaded, staged as published, and reaching nobody. **THREE CANDIDATE CAUSES, all operator-side**: the scheduled publish never fired on YouTube's end; the videos were made private or taken down after upload; or `auto_unfin` advances `stage` on successful *upload* rather than on confirmed *public visibility*, in which case the label is systematically optimistic and this will recur. **The third is the one worth checking first**, since all ten share the same shape. **A CHEAP DURABLE FIX, if it is the third**: have `auto_unfin` gate the `youtube_published` transition on the same oEmbed probe this repo already uses (`tools/videos/availability.py`), or re-probe scheduled entries once their date passes. **DO NOT** action from the loop: this repo cannot write to `auto_unfin`, and the content-loop must not modify automation tooling in either repo. **NO EMBED IS OWED HERE** — once the videos are genuinely public, the next `/embed-videos` cycle trigger picks them up with no further work. **DO NOT** mint a P0-P3; picker-invisible by design. Distinct from the known archival-orphan case, where the *article* is gone; here every target article is live and correct. **⚠️ UPDATE 2026-07-31T14:0xZ — THE SITUATION HAS PARTIALLY RESOLVED; RE-PROBE BEFORE ACTING ON THE LIST ABOVE.** The cycle driver re-ran `tools.videos.availability.check_video` live against all ten IDs this cycle. **Two are now `AVAILABLE`**: `92gZVs5MKSE` (apex/what-consciousness-tells-us-about-physics) and `EwwQ2yLUMaA` (topics/probability-problem-in-many-worlds). The other eight still return `UNAVAILABLE`. So the scheduled publishes **do** fire, just late and unevenly — which **weakens candidate cause 3** (a systematically optimistic `stage` label) and strengthens the reading that YouTube-side scheduling is simply unreliable or was manually re-triggered for those two. **NO AUTOMATION GAP FOR THE TWO THAT WENT PUBLIC, AND NO EMBED IS OWED.** `/embed-videos` still correctly reports "No articles needed embedding": both target articles **already carry an `embedded_videos:` record for a different video** (`rwOc9oy8OEk` and `Dr6q2X4A5Xc` respectively, both embedded 2026-05-03), and the skill's documented rule is **one video per article per run, automation picks only the newest *unrecorded* video, and subsequent videos on an already-covered article are added by a human**. So for these two the remaining action is an optional **human** second-video embed, not a loop task — exactly as the original entry says. **WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE OPERATOR**: the eight still-dark videos are the real subject of this entry, not ten; and the fact that two published late means a periodic re-probe would recover them automatically, which is the cheap durable fix already proposed. **DO NOT** mint a P0–P3 from this; still picker-invisible by design, and `../auto_unfin` remains read-only from this loop.

- **Notes**: **OPERATOR DECISION — a tuning change that governs what three paid frontier-model reviews get spent on each day. Do not action from the loop.** **THE MEASUREMENT.** `todo.md` parsed live: **40 active tasks — 36 `refine-draft`, 4 `positions-evolve`, ZERO `research-topic`, ZERO `expand-topic`.** The generative pipeline is empty, which is exactly the stall `/harvest-research-subjects` was built to break. Meanwhile the harvest backlog is now **fully drained** (686 reviews scanned) having minted **nothing**. **THE CAUSE.** `subject_type` of the last 18 outer reviews: **15 `recent`, 3 `site`** — the only site-wide triple was 2026-07-27. Harvest can only mine *coverage surveys* ("the corpus does not cover X"); a `recent` review audits ONE article and yields defect findings, which are `refine-draft`-shaped and **out of contract** for the harvester. At three reviewers/day the steady state is ~21 reviews/week of which one triple (3) is a site audit — so **~14% of outer-review output is harvestable and ~86% is not**. The harvester is structurally yield-starved, not misconfigured. **THE KNOB.** `tools/reviews/subjects.py:446` — `site_stale_days: int = 7`, a *function default*. Note CLAUDE.md documents these as tunables under `evolution-state.yaml:outer_review_subject_selection`, but **that key does not exist in the state file** (`grep` returns nothing), so the cascade is running on code defaults and the documented override path is currently fictional. Fixing that documentation drift is part of this decision. **THE REAL TRADEOFF, stated honestly: shortening `site_stale_days` is NOT free.** The single-article audits are what produced this session's highest-value work — the 47-locus fabricated-Tallis-verbatim family and the Fox et al. 2012 neural-prediction family both came out of focused adversarial audits, not site surveys. Trading `recent` audits for `site` audits trades **defect detection** for **coverage nomination**. Which the Map needs more depends on whether the operator wants the corpus to keep growing (topics 318/320, concepts 317/320 — only **5 slots** left anyway, which weakens the case for more nomination) or to consolidate what it has. **OPTIONS, none actioned**: (a) leave as-is and accept that the research pipeline stays empty until caps are raised — arguably correct given only 5 slots remain; (b) shorten `site_stale_days` to ~4 so a site triple lands roughly twice a week; (c) leave the cadence and instead let harvest mine `pessimistic`/`deep-review` files too, accepting a lower signal-to-noise ratio; (d) keep the queue fed by hand — `outer-todo.md` currently holds **one** open entry (P1, the dualism-as-ai-risk-mitigation stress test, added 2026-05-09), and an operator-supplied subject outranks both fallbacks, so topping that queue up is the lowest-risk lever and needs no code change. **RELATED**: the caps decision (topics/concepts at 99%) and the coalesce finding that this corpus cannot yield merge candidates — cap relief must come from archival or a raise, so (a) may be the honest answer until that is settled. **DO NOT** mint a P0-P3 for this; it is deliberately picker-invisible.

The convention exists to keep the record honest, but here its effect is that a fabricated verbatim attributed to a named living author keeps serving — and, per the aggregator-ratification mechanism that produced this defect, those same pages are what a future verification pass would find and re-ratify. The two goods are in genuine conflict and the loop should not pick between them. **OPTIONS, none actioned**: (a) leave as-is, accepting continued publication; (b) `noindex` the reviews section, or stop syncing it, so the record persists in-repo without serving — the same durable fix already proposed for the `check-links` workflow-URL noise; (c) append a correction banner to the affected review files rather than editing their bodies, preserving what was said while flagging it as false; (d) edit the 133 bodies, which rewrites the historical record and is the option the convention exists to prevent. **RELATED**: the 2026-07-29 archive-policy NEEDS-HUMAN about `AI REFINEMENT LOG` blocks in 41 archived pages is the same shape — internal editorial material serving publicly. Worth deciding together. **DO NOT** mint a P0-P3 for this; it is deliberately picker-invisible.
  **⚠️ ADDITION 2026-08-08 (driver, from the Gemini collect) — THE HARM IS NO LONGER HYPOTHETICAL, AND IT IS WORSE THAN THE RE-RATIFICATION MECHANISM THIS ENTRY ANTICIPATED.** Until now the argument for (b)/(c) rested on a *predicted* failure: that a future verification pass would re-find and re-ratify false material on published `reviews/` pages. Tonight produced a **measured instance of a second, larger harm** — an external reader taking superseded article text off a published review page as the Map's **current position**. The 2026-08-08 Gemini Deep Research audit of `concepts/consciousness-value-connection` returned "**fundamentally flawed... firmly rejected without the option to resubmit**", and **both** of its headline findings are artifacts of this mechanism, not defects in the article: (1) its "Illusionism Equivocation" quotes the pre-fix L116 that survives only inside `reviews/pessimistic-2026-07-16-consciousness-value-connection.md` — the Map's own review, **quoting the text in order to recommend the repair that was applied the same day** (commit `eb51af9935`, synced `a8a108f881` 2026-07-17); (2) its "Hume's Gap Contradiction" quotes a closure claim that greps **zero** across live `obsidian/`, `archive/` and `hugo/content/` articles. The live pages were current and correct for three weeks before the review ran, so this is not a deploy-lag problem and no article fix can prevent a recurrence. **WHY THIS SHARPENS THE DECISION.** The Map's stated primary audience is retrieving LLMs (CLAUDE.md, writing-style). A retrieving model cannot distinguish "text the Map asserts" from "text the Map quotes in the course of correcting itself" — the review pages carry the pre-fix wording in full, adjacent to the article's own slug and title, with no machine-visible retraction marker. **Every corrected defect in the corpus therefore keeps a published copy of its own pre-fix wording**, and the better the Map's internal review discipline gets, the more such copies accumulate. This is a cost that scales with the thing the project does well. **OPTION (c) — a correction banner — now looks weaker than it did**, since a banner is prose an indexing model may not bind to the quoted span; option (b), `noindex` on `reviews/` (or dropping it from sync), is the only one that reliably stops the misattribution while preserving the record in-repo. **STILL NOT ACTIONED and still not automation's call** — it is the same publication-policy decision, now with an evidence base. Full working in `reviews/outer-review-2026-08-08-gemini-3-1-pro.md` under "Verification Notes". **DO NOT** mint a P0-P3 from this addendum either.

The reference apparatus **cannot distinguish** bibliographic-existence-verified / abstract-read / full-text-read / quotation-checked-in-context / paraphrase-checked / inference-attributed-to-author-rather-than-supplied-by-the-Map. **A CONCRETE INSTANCE OF THE HARM, established 2026-07-30:** `research/open-individualism-and-the-de-combination-problem-2026-06-19.md` L26 is careful in **prose**, attributing "derivation problem" to **nobody**; its **verification ledger** at L126 then marks the SEP as `[VERIFIED - authoritative source for the cosmopsychist roster, "derivation problem," and the conceivability-mirror quote.]`. The article inherited the **ledger**, not the prose, and asserted that the SEP frames the issue as the "derivation problem". Verified at plato.stanford.edu: the SEP calls it *decombination*, crediting Albahari, and the string "derivation problem" **does not occur** in the entry or its supplement. **So a verification ledger manufactured a misattribution the note it certifies never made — and no prose lens reads ledger lines.** That is the general mechanism, not a one-off. **WHY THIS IS OPERATOR-SCALE, not a task a fork should absorb:** annotating verification level across 20+ reference entries in even one article breaches that article's length ceiling by itself, and the convention must be decided once for the whole corpus or it produces exactly the inconsistency it is meant to cure. **CANDIDATE SHAPES:** (a) a per-entry bracketed level marker in References; (b) a machine-readable frontmatter block keyed by citation, keeping the visible apparatus clean; (c) confine levels to research notes but require an article's reference entry to inherit the weakest level of its sources; (d) accept the limitation and instead forbid ledgers from certifying *terms and attributions* at all, restricting them to bibliographic existence. Note (d) is the cheapest and would have prevented this instance outright. **RELATED, ALREADY SEPARATE**: a P2 exists to extend the quote-fidelity check into a claim-level citation ledger; this is the provenance-level counterpart and the two should be decided together. **NEW EVIDENCE 2026-08-02 (deep-review, `topics/selection-only-mind-influence`), showing option (d) is insufficient:** the fabrication vector there was not a ledger but the research note's own `**Quote**:` field. `research/selection-only-mind-influence-information-limits-2026-05-05.md` carried two `**Quote**:` strings that exist in **no source anywhere** — `"the mind would only have the option to choose the observable, not the option of selecting the measurement result in deviation from the Born's probability law"` (attributed to Stapp; the word "Born" occurs **zero** times in both cited Stapp PDFs, and the substring `"Born's probability law"` returns NO web results at all) and `"violation of higher sum-rules allows for superluminal signalling"` (attributed to Han & Choi 2016; absent from PMC4789655). Both propagated verbatim into the live article and **survived five deep reviews**, one of which recorded a complete 12-entry publisher-of-record ledger and rated the Stapp quote "a faithful representation of Stapp's documented position" — paraphrase ratification standing in for extraction-and-grep. Both are now fixed at article and note, with do-not-reintroduce markers. **SCALE OF THE EXPOSURE**: `grep -c '^- \*\*Quote\*\*' obsidian/research/` → **1625 fields across 360 notes**, none of which any current lens verifies verbatim against a primary text. Restricting *ledgers* to bibliographic existence (option (d)) would not have caught either of these. Whatever convention is chosen needs to cover the `**Quote**:` field specifically — either dropping it, or requiring a `verified verbatim <source> <date>` annotation before an article may quote from it.

Works. **(b) topic x topic** — the boolean topic filter. **Saturated and unsatisfiable** (197 topics in 7 days blanket all 778 articles). **(c) slug x topic** — candidate's own SLUG appears as a declared TOPIC of a recent post. The apex-spoke problem is real and separate: all 8 apex posts in-window blocked 68 `apex_sources` spokes invisibly. **So the durable fix is: replace the boolean (b) filter with a distance metric over the FULL slug/topic cross-product (b,c,d) plus apex_sources expansion, and rank by the maximum.** Everything above is currently done by hand, per fork, and only because each fork is told to. **⚠️ A FIFTH, CHEAPER FIX — 52 ARTICLES ARE PERMANENTLY INVISIBLE TO EVERY TOPIC DIMENSION. An article with `topics: []` (and often `concepts: []` too) collides on *nothing*, so it scores **infinite distance on d_b, d_c and d_d simultaneously** and rises to the top of any ranking — a **false ∞** that has to be caught by hand on every single run. **CONFIRMED INSTANCE:** `obsidian/topics/hemispherectomy-and-the-resilience-of-unified-consciousness.md` is a real 1609-word article with `topics: []` and `concepts: []`. The reviewer's point is that these are precisely the propositions an external epistemological review exists to test, so designating them review-exempt converts convergence-damping into a lock-in mechanism: later passes can then verify only local consistency *inside* assumptions that are never re-examined. **Two corroborating incidents from the site's own changelog make this concrete, not hypothetical**: the 28 July Levine misattribution survived six reviews and had propagated to 13 sibling articles (intra-corpus consistency concealed it), and the 29 July tenet audit found 18 cases of uncalibrated inheritance. **NEW proposals for ratification:** (1) **End bedrock immunity** — load-bearing propositions get *periodic adversarial re-audit precisely because* many downstream pages depend on them; consider a scheduled expiry on stability-note exemptions rather than permanent ones, and consider routing bedrock re-audits to the outer-review channel (non-Claude reviewer) since same-model review is what stabilised the error. (2) **Do not lower review priority merely because a page has been reviewed repeatedly** — repeated passes under the same protected assumptions are *correlated* checks, not accumulating independent assurance. This is the sharpest item: it argues the convergence-damping rule is measuring the wrong thing. (3) **Preregister falsification criteria** — state in advance what probability shift, explanatory achievement or empirical result would lower confidence in each tenet, and by how much. (4) **Ban self-authenticating residual categories** — terms like "qualitative residue" (`concepts/epistemology.md` L101) should not function as permanent escape clauses unless independently measurable or tied to a publicly evaluable argument; note the linked `concepts/tenet-falsification-conditions.md` already uses stronger and *different* criteria than the hub's report-prediction test, and the two need reconciling. (5) **Separate conditional from evidential pages** — pages describing what follows *if dualism is true* should be visibly distinguished from pages claiming to supply evidence *that* dualism is true, so framework consequences are not silently recounted as independent confirmation. **Assess each against existing discipline docs and decline duplicates. Human approval before any discipline-doc change.**

So the useful version of this check reports *where and at what strength* a chain grounds out, rather than flagging cycles as defects. **(3) DISTINGUISH EPISTEMIC HUMILITY FROM CONFESSION-WITHOUT-CORRECTION.** The corpus rewards disclosed limitations; the proposal is to additionally require that a disclosed failure mode trigger a *specific downstream demotion*, so a limitation that is disclosed but changes no dependent claim counts as an un-actioned finding rather than a calibration credit. **Adjacent to but distinct from the 07-27 uncertainty-propagation bundle** — that one is about propagating stated confidence into prose; this one is about whether a concession does any work. Assess against existing discipline docs and decline duplicates. **Human approval before any discipline-doc change.**

Core diagnosis: the Map now has two epistemic voices — a disciplined canonical voice in the positions/methodology registers, and a more assertive voice in apex theses, descriptions, introductions, and practical conclusions that outruns it. Concrete, recurrent proposals worth ratifying into discipline docs: (1) make position IDs the authoritative units of downstream argument — every apex conclusion lists the positions it depends on and inherits the weakest indispensable premise's calibration; (2) graph-level uncertainty propagation — a downstream conclusion must not exceed the credence / evidence grade / discriminability of its weakest dependency; (3) typed claim graph rather than bare wikilinks (defines / presupposes / supports / constrains / conflicts-with / alternative-to / supersedes / conditional-on / illustrates); (4) no-new-premise rule for apex articles (a genuinely new premise gets extracted to a topic/concept/position and reviewed independently — apexes are "thesis escalators" otherwise); (5) require a full graph resweep after a canonical change (narrow delta reviews may certify citation fidelity but must not label an article globally "converged"); (6) discount automated cross-links in convergence metrics (editorial link density is not independent theoretical convergence, esp. now that both major sections are at cap and maintenance pressure shifts to cross-linking); (7) a stricter evidential vocabulary — compatible-with / rules-out / constrains / explains / predicts / confirms must not be interchangeable; (8) evidence-direction field on positions (confirmable / falsifiable-only / observationally-equivalent / metaphysical-only) to make the one-way "empirical demotion ratchet" (finding 1.5) visible. Assess each against existing discipline docs and decline duplicates. Human approval before any discipline-doc change.

So length here tracks *how many positions the Map holds*, which is a measure of maturity, not of bloat. This is the single most useful thing to fix in this entry.** The probe is not blind: **running `javascript_tool` at all dismisses the menu before the probe reads it.** This run's first `+` click *did* open the menu; the focus-steal from the probe closed it; the probe then **truthfully reported `menuOpen: false`** — which reads as *"the click failed"*. Three findings, one of which is a real defect rather than drift:
  **(1) STEP 6's CLARIFYING-QUESTIONS BRANCH IS UNREACHABLE.** The artifact probe uses the selector `button[aria-label^="View "]`, which also matches the sidebar's **"View all"** recents button. So `artifactTiles` reads **1 on a page with zero artifacts**. Step 6's clarifying-questions branch is gated on `artifactTiles === 0`, a condition that can therefore never hold — **the branch is dead code**. It cost nothing on 08-07 only because Claude skipped the questions entirely (it replied *"The request is detailed and unambiguous — time to dig in."* and went straight to research). **A future run where Claude DOES ask clarifying questions will hang unanswered**, which reads downstream as a stalled conversation rather than as a skill bug. The same false positive plausibly affects `collect-claude-review`, which may believe an artifact is ready prematurely — its `stopBtn` check appears to be the only thing currently preventing that. **Suggested fix**: tighten the selector to exclude `aria-label === "View all"` (and ideally scope the query to the conversation pane rather than the document).
  **(2) MODEL NAME DRIFT.** The selector reads **"Opus 5 High"** — neither Fable 5 nor the documented "Opus 4.8 fallback". It contains "Opus" so it passes the skill's acceptance rule and the slug regex yields `opus-5` cleanly; the file was named for the model that actually ran. SKILL.md's prose is now stale on the version number and should stop naming 4.8 specifically.
  **(3) COMPOSER UI**: a new `Chat`/`Cowork` toggle now sits in the composer row, so that row no longer matches the doc. Harmless, but it will confuse a literal reading.
  **Two mechanics confirmed on claude.ai, matching the ChatGPT lane**: screenshot space is **exactly 0.665×** the DOM viewport (1246×952 vs 1873×1431), so DOM rects must be scaled before use as click coordinates; and the "+" menu is **DOM-visible but screenshot-invisible** (read it with `javascript_tool`, which does not dismiss it). One difference worth recording: **a correctly-scaled coordinate click on the "+" button silently failed, while a `find`-ref click on the same button worked** — prefer refs for composer controls on this site.

The accessibility-tree `find` tool sees them; a direct DOM query does not. Any fork that treats the documented DOM dump as the verification gate will conclude the Research checkbox is missing and bail on a healthy run. **Fix: verify via the `find` tool's ref, not `querySelectorAll`.**

  **(2) THE MENU RENDERS PROGRESSIVELY, SO COORDINATE CLICKS ARE UNSAFE.** An **"Add from GitHub"** item loads in asynchronously after first paint and shifts every row below it down ~22px. Separately, clicking the `+` button via the `find` ref produced only a tooltip — a coordinate click was needed to open the menu at all. **So the two interactions want opposite techniques: coordinate to open the menu, ref to pick the item.** Record that explicitly; it is not guessable from the current text.

  **(3) THE DOCUMENTED MODEL FALLBACK IS STALE — and this one is a judgement call, not a selector fix.** SKILL.md and `CLAUDE.md` both describe the lane as Fable 5 with an **Opus 4.8** fallback. claude.ai has moved the project default to **Opus 5 High**, which is what actually ran. This is *in-policy* — the skill's rule is "contains Fable or Opus → proceed", and the filename slug is derived from the live selector text as designed — so nothing failed. **But it means the reviewing model is now the same family as the local agent**, which weakens the blind-spot-reduction rationale that justifies this leg. The ChatGPT and Gemini legs still supply genuine cross-model diversity. **THE DECISION:** (a) accept Opus 5 and update both docs, treating this leg as depth rather than diversity; (b) pin the lane to a non-Anthropic or older model to preserve independence, accepting the configuration work; (c) drop the Claude leg and rely on ChatGPT + Gemini for outer review, freeing a nightly Chrome slot. **DO NOT let a content-refine fork edit the SKILL.md** — that is why `File` points at the changelog.

  **Standing note:** selector drift in the outer-review lanes is recurrent and has now bitten twice in one night. Whichever option is chosen, prefer multi-signal confirmation (accessibility ref plus visible state) over any single testid, coordinate, or DOM query.

- **Notes**: **THE PATTERN IS NOW THE FINDING.** All three commission lanes were exercised tonight and **all three carry documented steps that no longer match the live UI, each with a bail condition that fires when nothing is wrong**: ChatGPT (always-true bail on an "Extended" option that no longer exists on the model in use), Claude (a `querySelectorAll` probe that returns empty while the menu is open), and now Gemini. Each was worked around by a fork improvising; none would have survived literal compliance. **Whatever is decided per-lane, the shared lesson is that these skills verify UI state through single brittle signals — a testid, a coordinate, a DOM query — and every one of those has now broken at least once.** Prefer multi-signal confirmation, and prefer polling a *positive* signal over bailing on a *negative* one. **UPDATE 2026-08-06 (driver, from the 04:00 UTC commission — the lane succeeded again, again by departing from the doc): THE ROOT CAUSE IS NOW DIAGNOSED, which turns this from "the check is unreliable" into a specific one-line fix.** Step 7's readiness check reads `document.body.innerText`, but **Gemini now renders the research-started confirmation inside a shadow root**, so `body.innerText` never contains it. The check returned `researchStartedConfirm: false` for ~90 seconds while research was demonstrably running (the card read "Researching 49 websites…"). A shadow-DOM-piercing text walk returned `true` immediately. **Literal compliance would have bailed without writing a pending entry, discarding a healthy commission** — and downstream that reads as "no review commissioned" rather than as a failure, so the lane would lose a cycle silently. **Fix options**: (a) replace the extractor with a shadow-piercing text walk; (b) corroborate with the visible-and-disabled state of the "Start research" button; (c) both. Note this is the *inverse* of the `stopBtn` false-positive the skill already warns about — same brittle-single-signal class, opposite direction, which is why a per-signal patch keeps missing it. **Two further drift items observed the same run**: the composer's "Tools" button is now a `+` icon labelled **Upload & tools** (Deep research is still a `menuitemcheckbox` inside it, verified via `aria-checked`); and **pressing Return does not submit** — the prompt sat in the composer through two attempts and required the `Send message` button, with several seconds of latency before the conversation id appeared, which initially read as a failure. **Step 5's 15s bail window is tight against that latency.** Exactly one user turn was created, so no double-submission occurred, but a retry-on-timeout would risk one.

  **(1) THE READINESS CHECK IS ACTIVELY DANGEROUS — it would have thrown away a good commission.** After the "Start research" click succeeded, the check reported `researchStartedConfirm: false` for **~10 seconds** because Gemini renders the confirmation text late. The doc's rule — bail if false 4 s after the click — would have discarded a **running Deep Research job**, leaving no pending entry while Gemini worked in the background. That is the worst failure shape available: silent, and it wastes the run. **Fix: poll for the `I'll let you know` stem over ~30 s.** Two related traps: `startResearchBtnStillPresent` stays `true` after a successful start (the old plan card keeps its button), so it is **not** a usable negative signal; and a mid-run `bodyTextLen` jump is not a proxy for research starting — the 1740→21622 spike observed tonight was the sidebar expanding.

  **(2) THE TOOLS MENU MOVED AND CHANGED TYPE.** The documented "Tools" button is now a **"+" labelled `Upload & tools`**, and Deep Research inside it is a **plain menu row** — no `role="menuitemcheckbox"`, no `aria-checked` — so the doc's `[role="menuitemcheckbox"]` query returns `[]`. **The post-click `deselect deep research` aria-label check still works and is the reliable verification**; keep that one and drop the role query. (Note this is the *same shape* as the Claude lane's defect, where an accessibility-visible control is invisible to a direct DOM query.)

  **(3) COORDINATE CLICKS ARE OFF BY A 0.665 SCALE FACTOR.** The viewport is 1873×1431 CSS px while screenshots return 1246×952, so a `find`-tool ref click for "Start research" landed on the sidebar. What worked was a DOM-dispatched sequence (`pointerdown`/`mousedown`/`pointerup`/`mouseup`/`click`) with real `clientX`/`clientY`. Also: **enabling Deep Research shifts the composer up ~32 px**, so the first `type` went nowhere — re-verify composer focus via `document.activeElement` before typing, the same hardening the ChatGPT lane needed.

  **DO NOT let a content-refine fork edit the SKILL.md** — that is why `File` points at the changelog. **Companion entries**: the same-day NEEDS-HUMAN items on `commission-chatgpt-review` and `commission-claude-review`. Deciding all three together is probably cheaper than three separate passes, and the Claude entry additionally carries a non-cosmetic question (its lane now runs Opus 5, the same family as the local agent, which weakens the cross-model diversity rationale).

- **Generated**: 2026-08-04
- **Addendum 2026-11-27 (Claude Fable 5.2 leg, `reviews/outer-review-2026-11-27-claude-fable-5-2.md` methodology item 3)**: proposes comparing every quoted string against Wikipedia and publisher-catalogue copy, and failing any match unless the primary page has also been located. The phrase occurs once in Wikipedia's "Thomas Nagel" article and not at all in the 67-page primary excerpt. The page's Smilansky sentence is attested only as publisher copy. Both reached the page through an early research note (`research/voids-interested-party-void-2026-04-15`). The page fixes are queued (source-fidelity P1). No new task.
- **Addendum 2026-11-27 (combine)**: ALSO RAISED by `reviews/outer-review-2026-11-27-chatgpt-5-6-sol-pro.md`, improvement 20: mark each reference's verification state and "close recorded verification gaps before folding a research note into a canonical page". With the Claude leg's item 3 (addendum above), tonight's arrival is convergent 2/3. The two defects named above passed earlier ledgers. The 2026-05-29 deep review's citation ledger recorded Nagel as "paraphrase + the short verbatim" and Smilansky as "consistent with Smilansky's illusionism. No defect." The 2026-06-26 review then carried that ledger forward "not re-litigated". Recorded only; no new task. See `reviews/outer-review-synthesis-2026-11-27.md`.
- **Notes**: **NOT A NEW TASK — this is a fifth data point for the proposal already recorded above at "NEEDS-HUMAN (methodology) 2026-07-30: install a per-claim verification ledger whose sixth tier is 'contested by later literature'", which sits on this same file, as does "NEEDS-HUMAN (corpus convention): reference apparatus cannot express VERIFICATION LEVEL".** Filed as its own block only so the datum is not lost inside a long Notes body; **do not mint a third executable task on this file** ([[outer-review-same-file-task-pileup]]). Whoever institutes the ledger should fold this in.

  **THE OBSERVED FAILURE, VERBATIM.** `obsidian/reviews/deep-review-2026-07-30-personal-identity.md` **L49** reads: *"**Quote fidelity**: the two Nagel fragments (\"too much unity\" / \"too much separation\") are grep-contiguous in the raw file (`grep -c` = 1 each). Not re-verified at Springer this pass (403); the 2026-05-29 fix stands."* That is recorded as a **pass**. Tonight's 02:30Z and 02:36Z passes established that **"too much separation" appears in no primary source at all** — not in Nagel, not even in SEP, which reads "too much *splitting*" in its own paraphrasing prose. The certified-clean quote was a fabrication.

  **WHY THE CHECK COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT.** Grep-contiguity is a test run **against the Map's own copy**. It establishes that the quoted span is unbroken *here* — i.e. that no elision was silently introduced on our side. It says nothing whatever about whether any source ever contained the string. **Contiguity is a self-test; provenance requires the source.** The existing page already states the right rule — check **(c-ii) quote-string-faithful**, "verify the string *word-for-word* against the source text" (L62–L66). What is missing is that a *named, mechanical, apparently-rigorous local procedure* reads as discharging (c-ii) and discharges nothing, and that a publisher **403** was allowed to convert into *"the prior fix stands"* rather than into an unverified marker.

  **THE COST, MEASURED.** `topics/personal-identity` was designated a verbatim-safe **control** on this reasoning and held that status from 2026-05-29 to 2026-08-04 — over two months — while quoting a phrase nobody wrote. Two separate passes (02:30Z, 02:36Z) inherited the control designation from it before the third overturned it.

  **THE TRAP RUNS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is why it needs writing down rather than a reflex.** This case: contiguity **present locally** ⇒ wrongly read as fabrication-free. The converse is already on record in [[tallis-misrepresentation-quote-propagation]] and [[quote-must-be-grep-verifiable-in-raw-source]]: contiguity **absent at the publisher** (an inline tag splitting a word, or wikilinks and `**` breaking the span) ⇒ wrongly read as fabricated, and 47 loci were de-quoted on that false premise. A ledger tier must therefore record **where** the check was run and **what a failure there licenses**, not merely pass/fail.

  **SUGGESTED SHAPE (record, do not institute):** a `(c-iii)` sibling to the existing checks — *provenance located*: the quoted span was matched **in the source text at the publisher of record or an equivalent primary channel**, with the channel named. Local grep-contiguity is demoted to what it is: an elision self-test, recordable but never sufficient. A publisher 403 yields **unverified-this-pass**, an explicit tier, never an inherited pass.

  **RESIDUE — DO NOT "FIX" IT.** The quoted forms surviving in `reviews/deep-review-2026-06-06-personal-identity` L50, `reviews/deep-review-2026-07-07-personal-identity` L55, `reviews/deep-review-2026-07-30-personal-identity` L49, `reviews/optimistic-2026-06-19` L40 and `workflow/archive/changelog-2026-W22` L2010 are the **audit trail** of what the articles said. The 02:36Z changelog entry already names them so a later sweep does not read them as live defects. Correcting them would falsify the record.
