- **Notes**: Sophie R. Allen 2022 (*European Journal for Philosophy of Science* 12(2), art. 28, doi 10.1007/s13194-022-00451-3) was read IN FULL on 2026-10-22 via its PhilSci-Archive manuscript and the published Springer HTML (Wayback). Twenty quotes were verified, with a negative control. Her argument: in any powers ontology, explicitly including identity-thesis powerful qualities, zombie conceivability yields zombie possibility only if physical powers produce phenomenal properties by "a contingent form of emergence which mimics the behaviour of categorical properties". She calls that "fairly implausible and unlikely". Without independent reasons she calls such an ontology "question-begging since it seems entirely motivated by the desire to make physicalism a contingent doctrine and to provide an ontology in which the conceivability argument applies". Supervenient and causal emergence hold with nomological necessity on a powers view, so they do not restore zombies. Non-physical phenomenal powers, epiphenomenal or causally efficacious, get her pure-powers treatment, and a world where the physical does not produce the phenomenal "is one where dualism is true", not a starting point for the argument. She notes that her argument does not make powers theories inconsistent with dualism, so DUALISM IS NOT REFUTED. The issue is circularity in the Map's own reasoning. WHY IT BEARS ON THE MAP: the Map holds identity-thesis powerful qualities (`concepts/causal-powers` L41, L75). It picks contingent governing laws over dispositional essentialism because a zombie world is conceivable (causal-powers L79; `topics/consciousness-and-the-metaphysics-of-laws-and-dispositions` L96-L102, L126, L142). So the ontology that keeps zombie worlds possible is selected by appeal to zombie conceivability, and the zombie argument is then counted toward dualism. OPTIONS: (a) give independent reasons for contingent psychophysical production, e.g. the legislation or quantum-anchor arguments at laws-page L84-L86 and L140-L146, and engage Allen on the laws page; (b) concede on causal-powers and the laws page that the governing-laws choice presupposes zombie contingency, so the zombie premise cannot count as independent support inside the Map's own ontology (matches `concepts/modal-epistemology` L121: zombie possibility "no longer counts as independent evidence" on the rival routes); (c) check whether "different laws are metaphysically possible with the same properties" (causal-powers L59) is coherent with the identity thesis, which Allen takes to fix causal role essentially. SECONDARY: Allen groups powerful qualities with Russellian monism, a rival the Map rejects, which would push the zombie argument's conclusion into Chalmers 2010's Russellian-monism disjunct. Whatever is decided, update modal-epistemology L127, which marks the question open, and the P-D1 register entry if its premise's standing changes. Do NOT let a fork resolve this in prose.

(a) It equates event-causal theory with physicalism, though an event-causal account can take the causing events to be mental. (b) It is a non sequitur. The normative relation (which side is at fault in a mismatch) is fixed by the intention's content whatever the causal relatum is, so agent causation adds a bearer of causal power, not the should. (c) Its sibling on `concepts/agent-causation` L71 ("a literal directedness event-causal accounts render metaphorical") was CUT in bb3d8edc54 (2026-10-12) as unargued boundary-substitution. Suggested NEW (+7): `Direction of fit does not by itself decide between them, because the *should* in an intention's fit comes from its content, whichever kind of cause carries it out. What the Map adds is the normativity argument above: if neural description does not yield that *should*, an event-causal story told wholly in neural terms leaves it out, while an interactionist or agent-causal story need not.` SECOND LOCUS, L81: OLD `When an agent acts, they exercise world-to-mind fit: they hold an intention whose content specifies a not-yet-actual state of affairs, and they cause that state to become actual. "Precisely" claims for agent causation a scene that an event-causal reading fits equally well. Suggested NEW (+7): `When an agent acts, they hold an intention with world-to-mind fit, whose content specifies a not-yet-actual state of affairs, and they cause that state to become actual. Agent-causal theorists read this as a substance exercising causal power; event-causal theorists read the same scene as the intention causing the outcome.` The L83 NEW's "between them" depends on the L81 NEW's two readings: install both, or adjust the pronoun. Keep L85 (the 09-16 fix of Searle's fit/causation pairing) untouched. Its "Searle … would say the latter" clause is a partially verified lead in the review and is not part of this task. ### P3: `concepts/direction-of-fit` L89 answers the biological objection as a "why it evolved" story; teleosemantics (Millikan 1995) is a theory of what content is

- **Notes**: LENGTH 2,001 by analyze_length on 2026-11-01 (concepts hard 3,500, gate `>=`). BUDGET +40 net including the reference line (the review measured +32). DEFECT: L89 OLD `**The biological objection**: Some argue direction of fit reduces to biological function. Beliefs have mind-to-world fit because organisms that form accurate representations survive; desires have world-to-mind fit because organisms that act on motivational states reproduce. On this view, direction of fit is an evolutionary story, not a mark of irreducibility. The Map's response: evolutionary function may explain *why* these structures exist without explaining *what they are*. The normative dimension—that beliefs *should* match reality—is not captured by the historical fact that accurate representation was adaptive.` The objection is unattributed and stated as an adaptive-history story, so the "why, not what" reply answers a strawman: teleosemantics is a theory of what content IS. SOURCE (verified verbatim 2026-11-01 in SEP "Teleological Theories of Mental Content", plato.stanford.edu/entries/content-teleological/): "According to teleological theories, the contents of mental representations depend, at least in part, on functions, such as the functions of the systems that use or produce them". §3.2 says Millikan's theory covers directive representations and "'pushmi-pullyu representations', i.e. of representations that are at once descriptive and directive". The available in-framework reply, also from SEP: "Teleological theories share the strategy of explaining the norms pertaining to mental content as deriving from so-called functional 'norms', which are regarded as descriptive rather than prescriptive." Suggested NEW (+22): `**The biological objection**: Teleosemantics holds that direction of fit is fixed by biological function. On Millikan's account a representation's content, and whether it is descriptive or directive, depends on the functions of the systems that use it, and some "pushmi-pullyu" representations are both at once (Millikan 1995). This is a theory of what direction of fit *is*, not only of why it evolved. The Map's response: function explains correctness and the possibility of malfunction, but teleosemanticists themselves treat functional norms as descriptive rather than prescriptive. Whether a descriptive norm is the *should* that beliefs bear toward truth is the step the account has not yet earned.` Before installing, re-check every Millikan gloss against a raw source (SEP §3.2 or the paper). The "functions of the systems that use it" wording paraphrases SEP's general statement and is not a verified Millikan quote, so do not put it in quotation marks. REFERENCE (+10): add `1. Millikan, R.G. (1995). Pushmi-pullyu representations. *Philosophical Perspectives*, 9, 185-200.` in alphabetical position, between Humberstone and Searle. Crossref verified the journal, volume, year and first page 185 (DOI 10.2307/2214217). The end page 200 comes from two secondary listings: confirm it at JSTOR or Crossref, or omit it. Do NOT cite SEP in the article; it is the verification source. Do not touch L91 (thermostat; bedrock) or L93. Humberstone and Smith stay reference-only. Selleri's OCCT 2014 review; primary not fetched): "in no way implies that the terms in question, or the expressions, the syntactical or grammatical turns, are not and cannot be translated: the untranslatable is rather what one keeps on (not) translating" (p. xvii). WRONG per SEP "Donald Davidson" §3.4 (fetched 2026-11-03): "It is this failure of uniqueness that Davidson terms the 'indeterminacy' of interpretation … It nevertheless remains an ineliminable feature of all interpretation"; Davidson rejected untranslatable LANGUAGES (§4.2 "the idea of an untranslatable language … cannot be given any coherent formulation"). SEP "Quine" §6.2: indeterminacy = "different ways of translating a language which are equally correct but which are not mere stylistic variants" (a surplus of translations, not a shortage). So "sit closer to Quine's pole" does not follow. Rewrite the face: Quine, no fact fixes which adequate manual is right; Davidson, no language could be untranslatable, though he accepts indeterminacy; the translator's felt sense that one rendering is THE right one is the datum. A mind holds beliefs in compartments that are never jointly active, so it cannot survey its beliefs for consistency, and a contradiction between compartments gives no felt sign until it is resolved. FOUR FACES: storage (access depends on why you ask), silence (contradictions are met only as they end; Lewis's beliefs changed "straightway" on noticing), census (consistency checking is computationally infeasible, Cherniak), sampling (two answers to the same question beat either alone, Herzog & Hertwig 2009 "crowd within"). - **Notes**: ADDENDUM 2026-11-14T11:17Z (driver, from obsidian/research/contextuality-as-computational-resource-2026-11-14.md): one more theorem-statement defect on this page belongs in this pass. L43 (count 1 at mint): "from the non-commutativity of the observable algebra". That is wrong as stated: a single qubit and the odd-dimensional stabilizer fragment have non-commuting observables yet admit noncontextual models. Kochen–Specker contextuality needs dimension >= 3 and a suitable set of observables, not non-commutativity alone. Fix it at the same grade as the other theorem repairs; the research note gives the wording. A separate P3 fold (Howard et al. 2014) on this page is SEQUENCED AFTER this task. All strings confirmed count 1 at HEAD d2b5a93ef0. Read each sentence in full before editing. (1) L35 "what result obtains for a given observable depends on which other observables are measured alongside it" and (2) L41 "need not yield the same value as": Kochen–Specker constrains hidden-variable VALUE ASSIGNMENTS. Any model that pre-assigns values must let A's value depend on whether it is grouped with B or with C, but quantum theory gives A the same statistics in every context. Restate both sentences as claims about models, not about measured results. (3) L51 "Operationally equivalent preparations can lead to different statistical predictions…" is backwards: operationally equivalent preparations give identical statistics BY DEFINITION. Spekkens's result is that no ontological model can represent them all by the same distribution over ontic states (arXiv quant-ph/0406166 abstract: "three no-go theorems for ontological models, each based on an assumption of noncontextuality"). Model the wording on `apex/post-decoherence-selection-programme` L103, which states it correctly. Then re-derive or cut the sentence after it ("that preparation is itself context-dependent…"), which leans on the wrong version. (4) L73 "provides *structural room*" and L77 "a structured, non-determined space": contextuality supplies no indeterminism. De Broglie–Bohm is deterministic AND contextual (the Map's own `concepts/quantum-probability-consciousness` L108 says so). Kochen–Specker (1967), anticipated by Bell (1966) via Gleason-type reasoning (the page already cites Mermin 1993, which tells this story), shows that no noncontextual 0/1 value assignment exists. So the measure can be fixed noncontextually and actual outcomes cannot. This is the measure/actuality split [[envariance]] draws for Zurek, now general. THE DEFECT: `positions/quantum-interface` P-Q2 (credence high) says "conscious selection acts within a corridor whose outputs are per-trial indistinguishable from unbiased Born statistics" and "only conditionals on the conscious state itself are free" (L68). So a machine whose logical state is open to quantum indeterminacy drifts from an identically prepared duplicate whether or not either is coupled. A machine whose logical state is closed to it offers the Map no coupling site at all (L80's own engineering point). Divergence therefore tracks indeterminism, and on P-Q2 it can never separate selection from chance. (1) OLD "so a coupled system should drift from a causally closed duplicate somewhere in its dynamics". Keep the expectation, but add that an uncoupled duplicate on the same indeterministic hardware drifts too, per-trial indistinguishably (link `[[positions/quantum-interface#^p-q2|P-Q2]]`). (2) OLD "[[tenets#^no-many-worlds|No Many Worlds]] removes the branching confound, since on an Everettian reading divergence is what branching produces anyway and the observation would discriminate nothing." Delete it, or restate it: single-world Born chance produces the same divergence, so rejecting Everett removes no confound for this test. (3) OLD "With both tenets in hand the test rises from merely compatible to suggestive, and becomes discriminating only once that mundane noise floor can be excluded". Restate it: the test grades coupling-eligibility (whether the hardware's logical state is open to indeterminacy), not coupling. The convergent outcome is informative only by that route. Separating selection from chance would need statistics conditioned on the conscious state, which `[[quantum-randomness-channel-llm-consciousness]]` L125 states as "a prediction, conditioned on conscious content, about those outcomes". (4) L84 OLD "open in the specific sense that a candidate test exists and nobody has run it". Align it with (3), e.g. "open in the specific sense that a test of coupling-eligibility exists and a test of coupling would need content-conditioned statistics". KEEP the inversion-of-Cutter's-arithmetic point if it is restated inside his idealisation, and keep L80's circularity answer and L84's calibration hedges untouched. ai_system: append the executing fork's own model id only if it is ABSENT anywhere in the string. Line numbers are as at mint; re-grep each before editing. The evidence for every item is in the review file's critical list and citation ledger.
  (1) L125, L169, L177: Hegel holds the series has a terminus, so "transcendence is never complete" reverses him. See *Phenomenology* Introduction, Baillie trans. 1910 vol. 1 p. 81: "The terminus is at that point where knowledge is no longer compelled to go beyond itself".
  (2) L123: the quoted line "the second you realize you are limited … frees you of those barriers" is not Hegel's and has no source. Hegel's own sentence is on p. 81: consciousness "immediately transcends what is limited".
  (3) L70–71: L70 is correct (Albert coined the name). "Directly formalises" at L71 overstates; the trilemma is an informal argument against ultimate justification. Also note that Albert's own answer is the principle of critical testing (*Traktat* ch. II §5).
  (4) L73: the "Quote" is Wikipedia's own sentence, not Albert's. Relabel it.
  (5) L79: TLP 6.54 concerns "My propositions", which are *recognised* as nonsensical; they do not "become nonsensical".
  (6) L84 and L81: the wording is the 1998 revised Winch translation (p. 10e). The 1980 Winch reads differently ("if the place I want to get to could only be reached by way of a ladder").
  (7) L90, L91, L92, L94: these are the 2025 *Fists Full of Sand* blogger's own sentences and glosses. They are not a tradition's analysis, not Nanyue's metaphor, and not practitioners' reports. Nanyue's target was Mazu sitting in meditation to become a Buddha.
  (8) L105, L212: the No Many Worlds inference is a non sequitur. Branching copies a mind and does not pool its capacities.
  (9) L101–L102: the phrasing is the ResearchGate paper's and needs credit. "Self-referential loops introduce blind spots" is loose; the relevant result is Gödel's second theorem.
  (10) L115: "energy metabolism sets hard limits" is unsupported. The 20%/2% figure is in Herculano-Houzel 2011 (*PLoS ONE* 6(3) e17514).
  (11) L59: "a form of blindness — to consciousness, to value, to personhood" is unverified against the book. Replace it with the OUP description's formulation.
  (12) L62: the Nagel "Quote" ("There is no view from nowhere, only the aspiration toward it") is unverified and probably not Nagel's. Mark it UNVERIFIED.
  (13) L129–L136 and L239: the SSRN paper is a framework for technologically induced cognitive diminishment (TICD). The AI recursive-self-improvement and "fixed human processing speed" points are unverified as its content. The correct title has "for the Technologically Induced"; the version of record is *J. Cognitive Enhancement* 9(3) 346–359, doi 10.1007/s41465-025-00331-7.

  EVIDENCE (checked 2026-11-26): L48 "Phenomenologists call this *for-me-ness* (Dan Zahavi)" and "each conscious state carries an implicit tag"; L54 "accompanies every conscious state" and "constitutive of the experiential character of conscious states from the outset". If the feature is constitutive of every conscious state, a conscious state that lacks it is exactly what needs argument. Guillot 2017 (*Rev. Phil. Psych.* 8, 23–53, DOI 10.1007/s13164-016-0313-4; abstract verified at OpenAlex) separates for-me-ness, me-ness and mineness and finds "no conceptual implication from for-me-ness to me-ness or mineness". The Map's own `concepts/thought-insertion` L80 already says this page must adopt that split: "with her three, the claims are consistent: for-me-ness universal, mineness general but able to lapse."
  (1) §Defining the Feature: install Guillot's split. For-me-ness is first-personal givenness, constitutive on Zahavi's view. Mineness is presentation-as-mine, the separable feature this page studies. Scope L48's "each conscious state carries an implicit tag" to the ordinary case. Cite Guillot through a zero-word piped link to [[thought-insertion]], which carries Guillot 2017, or add a reference entry only if it is funded.
  (2) L74, the report-coherence argument ("If mine-ness were not separable, DPD would be impossible to describe…"): once the split is in, the report needs for-me-ness (first-person access), and mineness is what is degraded. Rewrite the argument so it shows mineness is separable from for-me-ness, not from "the bare having of experience".
  (3) L108: bring "Depersonalisation shows that mine-ness can vanish" to the verdict in [[depersonalisation]], whose description calls the result "a defensible architecture claim with no metaphysical significance yet". Billon's case is abductive and graded, so DPD reports are compatible with degraded mineness.
  (4) THE VOID. The page claims both separability (from clinical variation) and constitutive inaccessibility (L110 "you cannot get behind ownership to explain it, because ownership is presupposed by every explanation"; L50 "a structural limit rather than a gap in knowledge awaiting research"; L120 "structurally inaccessible from within"). This is a dilemma. If the void concerns constitutive for-me-ness, the presupposition argument may hold, but the DPD evidence, which concerns mineness, does not bear on it. If the void concerns separable mineness, its causes can be studied contrastively by third-person methods (perturbation, lesion, computational models), and introspective opacity is not explanatory closure. Narrow the void to a first-person contrast / introspective-access limit and keep "from within". Either remove L50's "rather than a gap in knowledge awaiting research" or argue for it. L114 ("the ownership void is not one void but several"): this follows only on the phenomenal reading of type-specific relations, which L92 concedes Knappik does not grant, so make it conditional.

### P2: agentic-social topic-dedup has saturated — the selector pool has collapsed to a tiny empty-topics residue
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: .claude/skills/agentic-social/scripts/agentic_social_api.py
- **Status**: blocked (diverted from Active by the cycle driver 2026-07-28 — the notes say "operator's design call, do not pick unilaterally" and list five mutually exclusive options; the loop would have executed it as a refine-draft and picked one. Not an outage: posting works, URL-fallback degrades gracefully.)
- **Notes**: FOUND by the run-11910 `/agentic-social` fork after the driver asked it to investigate a fourth consecutive empty-`topics` selection; **independently driver-reproduced against live state**. **THE MECHANISM** is at `agentic_social_api.py:456`: `if article_topics and recently_posted_topics:` — an article whose `topics` frontmatter is **empty** short-circuits the overlap check and therefore *can never be filtered out*, while every article that HAS topics is tested against a ban set that now holds **221 topics accumulated from 154 recent posts**. **DRIVER-VERIFIED NUMBERS (live, run 11910)**: 784 candidate articles scanned; a faithful replay of the filter leaves **14 survivors, 12 of them empty-topics (86%)** against an empty-topics base rate of ~9% (71 of 810 articles carrying a `topics` field). The fork's own instrumented count, which also applies the index-page/sidecar guards the driver's cruder replay let through, put the survivor count at **1**. Both figures describe a collapsed pool; the 86%-vs-9% over-representation is the robust signal, and four consecutive empty-topics picks at random would be ~2e-5. **SELF-REINFORCING**: each empty-topics post contributes zero topics back to the ban set, so the set never ages out through variety, and `mark-posted` is legitimately called without `--topics` (correct behaviour — inventing topics would corrupt dedup — but it means topic-level dedup now receives no signal at all). **THE FAILURE MODE IS ALREADY DOCUMENTED IN THE CODE** at lines 373-402, which anticipates it almost exactly ("once the 7-day topic-dedup filter empties the real-article pool… they become the sole primary-loop survivor and the selector returns them forever") and adds guards for `_`-prefixed files, `stem == parent.name`, `-index`/`-articles` suffixes, and an explicit `social_eligible: false` opt-out. **Those guards treat the symptom** (off-voice index pages reaching the network) **rather than the cause** (topic-dedup saturating). There is a URL-only fallback at :466 when `available` is empty, so this degrades rather than hard-fails — which is why it has gone unnoticed. **OPTIONS — operator's design call, do not pick unilaterally**: (a) expire the topic ban list on a much shorter window than the 7-day URL window (a few days of topics, not 154 posts' worth) — probably the smallest correct fix; (b) cap the ban-set size, evicting oldest first; (c) require overlap above a threshold (e.g. ≥2 shared topics, or a Jaccard floor) rather than rejecting on any single shared topic — note many articles share one broad topic like `consciousness`, which is likely what saturates the set; (d) backfill `topics` frontmatter on the ~71 bare articles, which fixes the short-circuit asymmetry but not the saturation; (e) make the empty-topics case explicit rather than implicit — an article with no topics should arguably be *ineligible* or *neutral*, not *always-eligible*. **DO NOT** simply delete the ban list or widen it to zero days — 7-day URL dedup alone would allow near-immediate thematic repetition, which is what topic dedup exists to prevent. Posting continues to work correctly in the meantime; this is a content-variety defect, not an outage.
  📏 **MEASUREMENT-ONLY ANNOTATION BY /replenish-queue 2026-08-19 00:45Z — STATUS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED, still blocked, still the operator's design call. Nothing here unblocks it.** Posting a fresh measurement because a P3 task elsewhere in the queue was citing this entry as evidence of a live failure mode, and the condition it describes no longer reproduces. Calling `get_published_articles()` directly from `agentic_social_api.py` returns a candidate pool of **676 articles of which ZERO have an empty `topics:` list** — the "tiny empty-topics residue" in this entry's title is now empty in the other direction. Three guards added since 2026-07-28 account for it, and the module's own comments narrate their history: the `stem == parent` section-index skip, the `stem.endswith(("-index", "-articles"))` skip, and the `social_eligible: false` opt-out honoured at L432-436. Directory scope does the rest — `CONTENT_DIRS` (L49-53) is only `concepts`, `topics`, `apex`, so the 11 empty-topics files that live under `voids/` and `positions/` were never candidates at all. **Option (d) in the list above — backfill `topics` on the bare articles — is therefore no longer load-bearing for this defect**; it survives only as cosmetic metadata hygiene and is tracked separately at P3. Options (a), (b), (c) and (e) concern ban-set saturation, which this measurement does **not** speak to and which may well still be live. **A human should decide whether that residual saturation question keeps this entry open or closes it.**

### Durable fix (NEEDS DEV — not loop-pickable): sync.py must delete orphaned hugo/content files on archive
- **Type**: operator/dev (code change) — do NOT pick as refine-draft; this is a `scripts/sync.py` / `tools/sync/converter.py` change for the operator.
- **Notes**: Root cause of the recurring [[coalesce-stale-hugo-duplicate-urls]] / [[archival_link_rot]] bug. When an article is archived/coalesced its obsidian source moves to `archive/<sec>/` (which syncs to `hugo/content/archive/<sec>/`), but sync NEVER deletes the original git-tracked `hugo/content/<sec>/<slug>.md`. That orphan keeps serving the full, un-flagged, STALE body at the original URL and shadows the Netlify 301 in `_redirects` (a non-forced redirect loses to a matching static file). **BULK CLEANUP DONE 2026-06-22 (this cycle, commit via auto(refine-draft)):** deleted 317 verified-safe orphans — 160 topics / 58 concepts / 97 voids, plus the 2 ChatGPT-flagged pages (evidential-weight-of-voids, causal-delegation). Every one had a `_redirects` 301 whose target resolves to a LIVE obsidian page (verified 315/315 redirect-present + 0/315 dead-target; a clean `rm -rf public && hugo` build confirmed the deleted URLs are absent (→ 301) while every replacement page still builds; re-sync does not recreate the orphans). **DURABLE FIX still needed:** make sync delete any `hugo/content/<sec>/<slug>.md` whose `obsidian/<sec>/<slug>.md` source no longer exists (it was archived/deleted), GATED on a `_redirects` rule existing for that URL so it can never create a 404. Until shipped, every future `/archive` or `/coalesce` re-introduces one stale duplicate (cf. the 2026-06-14 single-file precedent: the quantum-measurement-interpretations-beyond-mwi removal task).

### NEEDS-HUMAN (methodology ratification) 2026-09-07: the citation-ledger inheritance rule let two phantom references survive four publisher-of-record verification passes — evidenced, not hypothetical
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Status**: blocked (changes a standing verification discipline; do not adopt unilaterally)
- **File**: obsidian/project/calibration-audit-triple.md
- **Source**: outer-review
- **Review file**: `reviews/outer-review-2026-09-06-chatgpt-5-6-sol-pro.md`
- **Generated**: 2026-09-07
- **Notes**: **This is the reviewer's improvements #18 and #19, and unlike most methodology proposals from outer reviewers it arrives with a verified failure to point at.** ⚠️ **The concrete defects are already minted as executable tasks (one P1 on `topics/psychedelics-and-the-filter-model`, one P2 on `project/calibration-audit-triple` L495) — this entry is the *policy* question only. Do not duplicate those fixes here.** **The evidence.** The 2026-08-27 deep review of `topics/psychedelics-and-the-filter-model` recorded, in its Citation Web-Verify section (L53 of `reviews/deep-review-2026-08-27-psychedelics-and-the-filter-model.md`): "The remaining 23 entries are unchanged since the 2026-06-03 full publisher-of-record ledger (re-confirmed 2026-06-19 and 2026-07-07); that ledger stands." Under that rule an entry is owed re-verification only if it *changed*. Two entries in that unchanged set are phantoms, verified as such during this review's processing: reference 23 ("Timmermann, C. et al. (2024). DMT alters cortical travelling waves…", no such publication; the real paper is Irrmischer et al. 2026, *J. Neurosci.* 46(2):e0344252025) and reference 9 ("Hameroff, S. (2024) … Cambridge University Press", where the volume is Gao ed., **Oxford**, **2022** and the chapter title does not exist). Both were present on 2026-06-03 and therefore inherited, unchecked, through **four** passes. The same section's L47 shows the deep review *did* touch Timmermann, Mason and Lebedev — but only to trim **recitation redundancy**, never to check what the sources say. A third instance sits at `project/calibration-audit-triple.md` L495, inside the audit specification's own worked exhibit. **The policy question for the operator.** The inheritance rule is what makes the ledger affordable; removing it makes every deep review re-verify ~24 entries. Three options, in ascending cost: **(a)** keep inheritance but make it *tuple-scoped* — an unchanged entry is still owed a one-shot existence check of the (author, year, title, container, volume/pages, DOI) tuple against Crossref, which is cheap and would have caught both phantoms, while the expensive part (does the source support the claim?) stays owed only on change. **(b)** Additionally require, on any entry whose *body claim* is edited — as L47's recitation trim did — that the claim be re-checked against the abstract even if the reference entry itself is untouched; this is the seam that let an editorially-touched citation keep an unverified claim. **(c)** The reviewer's fuller #19: a literature-drift gate for fast-moving empirical pages, searching from the date of the last full empirical audit forward and forbidding ledger inheritance outright on such pages. Note the Map already runs a weekly `literature-drift-review` (Audit One of the triple), so (c) may be partly built — **check what that skill already covers before commissioning new machinery**, and note it audits one article per run, which is a different cadence from a per-pass gate. **Caution against over-reading**: the reviewer's own framing of the Map's review record is partly its own reconstruction, and several 2026 papers it cites are unverified aggregator chips (see the review file's `## Verification Notes`). The *ledger-inheritance* finding stands on this repo's own record, independently of anything the reviewer got right about the literature. **Related open entries** — read before ratifying, they may compose or conflict: `NEEDS-HUMAN (methodology ratification) 2026-09-02` on binding status changes, and `NEEDS-HUMAN (methodology ratification) 2026-08-06` on gates-vs-lenses (the same "does this become a blocking gate?" question, previously answered conservatively). **⚠️ CONVERGENCE 2026-09-07 — a second, independent reviewer now names this same policy defect.** The Claude Opus 5 leg of the *same* cycle (`reviews/outer-review-2026-09-06-claude-opus-5.md`, site-wide item #5) reached the ledger-inheritance finding without seeing the ChatGPT leg, and independently re-derived the Reference 23 chimera and the Lebedev misattribution that evidence it — so this is genuine corroboration, not one reviewer's hobby-horse, and it raises the case for ratifying rather than deferring. **Two formulations from that leg are worth carrying into the decision, because they sharpen option (a):** (i) verify the citation **as a tuple** — (author, year, title, container, volume/pages, DOI) checked *together* rather than field-by-field, on the reasoning that Reference 23 was a title-from-paper-A + venue-and-finding-from-paper-B fusion in which **every field was individually plausible** and only the combination was false, so a field-by-field check cannot catch this class; and (ii) state the inheritance bar directly — **a review pass may not inherit a previous pass's verification without re-checking the raw record** — with the specific diagnostic that *any citation whose components trace to two different DOIs is a hard fail*. That reviewer also names the structural reason the pipeline is prone to it: plausible metadata assembled from adjacent sources, then a Claude-on-Claude review loop that re-ratifies a prior ledger's "verified" stamp instead of re-deriving it from the artefact. **No new task was minted for this** — the concrete fixes are already queued and this entry remains the single policy question.

  **ADDENDUM 2026-09-29 (combine-outer-reviews — a second evidenced instance of the inheritance failure, this time on a philosophical quotation, at 2/2 productive legs).** Both same-day legs on `topics/constitutive-exclusion` found that L44's Merleau-Ponty "quotation" ("We are both a part of the world and coextensive with it, constituting but also constituted") is the IEP author's unquoted prose glossing PP 453 — and the ledger certified it: `reviews/deep-review-2026-07-15-constitutive-exclusion` L40 recorded it as "Verbatim at PP 453 (confirmed via IEP and independent secondary source)" and `reviews/deep-review-2026-09-10-constitutive-exclusion` L109 inherited that as "publisher-verified verbatim on 2026-07-15. **Not re-litigated.**" The stamp came from a secondary source and was then fenced by a stability note — the mechanism the 2026-07-29 "End bedrock immunity" entry describes. **ChatGPT 5.6 Pro** improvement 18: *"automated verification should fail when a direct quotation has only a whole-book reference"*; **Claude Opus 5.5** recommendation 16: *"flag any quote first found in a secondary source (IEP, SEP, Goodreads, quote aggregators) as 'quoted in'"*. The concrete fix is the open P1 on the article (which also corrects the 09-10 ledger); this entry remains the policy question, now with two evidenced instances (phantom references, 09-07; laundered quotation, 09-29). Cluster 1 / M1 of `reviews/outer-review-synthesis-2026-09-29.md`.

### ✓ 2026-05-25: Acknowledge dual-process / continuous-signal-detection contestation in memory-anomalies
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Pessimistic review 2026-05-19d Issue 3. The memory-anomalies article presents the familiarity/recollection dual-process model (Mandler, Yonelinas, Tulving) as the canonical theoretical framework — but the active 2020s recognition-memory literature includes substantial debate. Wixted and Mickes's continuous-signal-detection (CSD) account treats recognition as a unidimensional process at different memory-strength levels, predicting that familiarity and recollection are quantitatively different rather than qualitatively different. Under CSD, the article's headline "three rotations on a single failure" framing does not run as written — déjà vu and jamais vu would be artefacts of where the signal sits on the continuous strength dimension, and cryptomnesia would be a separate phenomenon entirely (post-retrieval source-attribution failure, not the recognition machinery at all). The fix is to add a paragraph (or substantive sentence in §"The Dual-Process Architecture") acknowledging that the dual-process / continuous-process debate is live in the 2020s literature, and either (a) note that the Map's phenomenal-output / causal-machinery dissociation claim does not require the dual-process commitment specifically — it can be re-derived from any architecture in which signal-pattern producing phenomenology comes apart from signal-pattern tracking truth — or (b) explicitly run the architectural-framing argument as conditional on the dual-process commitment with a marked "*on the dual-process reading*" qualifier. Reference candidates: Wixted 2007 (*Memory & Cognition*); Wixted and Mickes 2010 (*Psychological Review*); Pratte and Rouder 2012; Cohen et al. 2013. See `reviews/pessimistic-2026-05-19d.md` §"Critical Issues" Issue 3.

### ✓ 2026-05-25: Add MWI counterfactual-exclusion checklist across agency, death, quantum, machine-consciousness articles
- **Type**: refine-draft

That repair matters because Tenet 5 (Occam's-razor limits) would otherwise undercut anti-MWI arguments based mainly on ontological extravagance. Downstream articles still sometimes treat MWI as if it would straightforwardly fail phenomenologically or empirically, when the better formulation is: MWI can often provide a branch-local restatement of the data; the Map rejects what it does to indexical identity, actuality, and selection. ### ✓ 2026-05-25: Tighten O'Brien-Kop puruṣa parallel in epistemology-of-convergence-arguments
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Outer-review 2026-05-23 Claude Opus 4.7 §2 (O'Brien-Kop reading is one-sided). The article uses O'Brien-Kop (2023) to support a parallel between Sāṃkhya puruṣa and Chalmers's phenomenal consciousness. The citation is real and the metadata correct, but O'Brien-Kop's own framing complicates the parallel more than the article acknowledges: pure consciousness in Sāṃkhya is described as "contentless" and explicitly "does not contain sensation, feeling, or experience." Verified via secondary sources summarising the paper. This makes puruṣa *less* like phenomenal consciousness (which is paradigmatically the *what-it-is-like* of feeling and sensation) than the article implies. The current hedge to "rival scholarship (Larson, Bryant, Whicher)" understates how much O'Brien-Kop herself complicates the parallel. Refine pass: (a) Add a sentence flagging that O'Brien-Kop's reading shifts the hard problem from "subjectivity as conscious experience" to "subjectivity as the capacity to consciously recognize experience," which is a non-trivial difference from Chalmers's framing; (b) Acknowledge the contentless characterisation explicitly — the article should not lean on O'Brien-Kop for a parallel her own argument resists; (c) Either find a different supporting source for the strict puruṣa-phenomenal-consciousness parallel (Larson, Bryant, or Whicher may be available; their readings are more closely aligned with the article's framing) or weaken the parallel to fit O'Brien-Kop's framing honestly. Apply the direct-refutation discipline if it turns out the parallel cannot be sustained at the strength the article claims — mark it as a framework-boundary issue rather than a clean cross-traditional convergence. Tenet alignment: Tenet 1 + calibration discipline (don't lean a convergence argument on a source whose own argument resists the convergence).

### ✓ 2026-05-25: Rescope or substantively engage canonical convergence literature in epistemology-of-convergence-arguments
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Outer-review 2026-05-23 Claude Opus 4.7 §1 (Scope misframing) and §4 (Literature gaps). The title promises "the epistemology of convergence arguments" — a general epistemological analysis — but the article delivers a defense of a Swinburne-style cumulative case applied to consciousness/dualism. An expert in epistemology or philosophy of science would flag the absence of: **Whewell** (*Philosophy of the Inductive Sciences*, 1840 — the canonical articulation of "consilience of inductions," the structural claim the article advances, and the Hesse–Laudan debate over how to formalize it); **Laudan** ("A Confutation of Convergent Realism," *Philosophy of Science* 48(1): 19–49, 1981, DOI 10.1086/288975 — locus classicus for the very phrase "convergent realism" and the pessimistic meta-induction); **Psillos** (*Scientific Realism: How Science Tracks Truth*, Routledge 1999 — standard contemporary treatment); **Bovens & Hartmann** (*Bayesian Epistemology*, OUP 2003 — canonical formal treatment of convergence from "partially reliable independent witnesses"); **Blackwell–Dubins merging of opinions**, **Gaifman–Snir convergence-to-the-truth**, washing-out-of-priors; **Salmon** on common-cause explanation (directly relevant to the article's "common-cause-null" gesture, see separate task on that); **Sober** on the law of likelihood; **Lipton** (*Inference to the Best Explanation*, 2nd ed., Routledge 2004); **Stanford** (*Exceeding Our Grasp*, OUP 2006, on the problem of unconceived alternatives — directly relevant to the article's claim that no rival explanation of cross-cultural patterns is available); **Peirce** on convergence to truth in the long run; **Condorcet** jury theorem; and consensus-as-marker-of-reliability literature (Solomon, Beatty, Moss). Refine pass should choose between two paths: (a) **rescope** — retitle to something like "A Cumulative Case for the Irreducibility of Consciousness" or "Cross-Traditional Convergence and the Hard Problem," which is what the article actually argues; or (b) **expand** — add substantive sections engaging at minimum Whewell, Laudan 1981, Bovens & Hartmann 2003, plus the Bayesian convergence-of-opinion theorems. Option (a) is cheaper but cedes the more ambitious framing; option (b) lifts the article to a genuine contribution to the convergence-epistemology literature. The editor decision belongs in the changelog. Apply the direct-refutation discipline. Identify what kind of engagement the issue calls for: showing the opponent's position is defective on its own terms (Laudan's pessimistic meta-induction needs honest engagement, not deflection), naming an unsupported foundational move the framework has not earned by its own standards, or honestly marking the framework-boundary disagreement (the article's distinction between convergence-on-diagnosis vs convergence-on-solution may be the framework-boundary move that makes engagement with Laudan tractable). Apply the corresponding reply mode in **natural journal-quality prose** — see [[writing-style|the writing-style guide]]'s "Engaging Opponents in Journal-Quality Prose" section. **Do not expose mode labels in the article body.** Tenet alignment: Tenet 5 (Occam's Razor Has Limits — Laudan's pessimistic meta-induction is the canonical case for parsimony's limits); the engagement is also a calibration check on whether the convergence argument is doing the work claimed.

### ✓ 2026-05-24: Fix fabricated and conflated Barrett citation in epistemology-of-convergence-arguments
- **Type**: refine-draft

### ✓ 2026-05-19: Write topic article on Memory-System Vulnerability Hierarchies as Interface Evidence
- **Type**: expand-topic

The hierarchy is one of the catalogue's most underdeveloped strengths: it is a *graded* prediction the filter theory makes ("an interface with multiple channels is partially blocked") that production theories struggle to predict (they would predict uniform loss). A dedicated topic article would map the hierarchy across (a) anaesthesia (anoetic preserved, noetic disrupted, autonoetic severed) — Tulving's framework + the anaesthesia-recovery literature; (b) sleep stages (NREM-2 disrupts autonoetic, REM partially restores noetic-autonoetic, dreams produce noetic-only narratives); (c) hemispherectomy preservation patterns (which channels return after hemispheric reorganisation; the surprising preservation in adult-onset cases); (d) terminal lucidity (which channels return in the last hours/days — the catalogue's strongest exhibit of selective channel-restoration); (e) dissociative states (DID's compartmentalised autonoetic access; dissociative amnesia's selective autonoetic blockade with noetic preserved). The philosophical work: graded-vulnerability-with-separable-channels is a *stronger* filter-prediction than the single-binary-extinction reading — production theories must additionally account for *why these channels degrade in this order*, while filter theory predicts the ordering directly from differential channel-bandwidth and reconstruction-cost. Should explicitly engage the rival predictive-processing reading (which can also produce graded predictions through hierarchical-prior reweighting) and locate the disagreement at where each framing predicts the ordering from. ### ✓ 2026-03-16: Research Wheeler's participatory universe and "it from bit"
- **Type**: research-topic
- **Notes**: The apex's reverse inference connects to Wheeler's programme but goes further. Research: (1) Wheeler's delayed-choice experiments and temporal ontology implications. (2) "It from bit" — information more fundamental than matter. How relates to the Map's "actuality from consciousness"? (3) "Participatory universe" — observers necessary for universe to exist. The Map is more modest (consciousness selects outcomes, not creates reality). (4) Wheeler's 20 questions analogy. (5) Zurek's response (quantum Darwinism) — objectivity without observers. (6) Fuchs's participatory realism as heir to Wheeler. Position the Map relative to Wheeler: more specific, more modest, more constrained by tenets. Target: research note.
- **Output**: Wheeler's participatory universe and "it from bit"

### ✓ 2026-03-16: Research the Born rule — derivation attempts and their limits
- **Type**: research-topic
- **Notes**: The apex claims the Born rule is an interface specification not derivable from physics alone. Research major derivation attempts and their structural limits: (1) Gleason's theorem — assumptions, does it presuppose measurement? (2) Deutsch-Wallace decision-theoretic derivation within MWI — circularity objections. (3) Zurek's envariance — presupposes Born probabilities via decoherence? (4) Caves-Fuchs-Schack (QBism) from Dutch-book coherence — what does it prove? (5) Masanes-Müller information-theoretic axioms. (6) Saunders on probability in MWI. For each: what achieved, what assumed, does it address the first-person probability gap from quantum-probability-consciousness? Directly supports the apex's core claim. Target: research note.
- **Output**: the Born rule — derivation attempts and their limits

### ✓ 2026-03-16: Research bi-aspectual ontology and dual-aspect traditions
- **Type**: research-topic
- **Notes**: The apex "What Consciousness Tells Us About Physics" claims reality has two aspects: structure (wavefunction) and actuality (consciousness). Research the philosophical landscape. Key targets: (1) Spinoza's dual-aspect monism — how does the Map's view differ? Spinoza's aspects are of one substance; the Map commits to genuine dualism. (2) Pauli-Jung dual-aspect monism — psychophysical complementarity, unus mundus. (3) Chalmers' naturalistic dualism and the "structure and dynamics" argument from The Conscious Mind. (4) Nagel's Mind and Cosmos — physics incomplete without consciousness. (5) Russellian monism — physical structure is extrinsic, consciousness is intrinsic nature. How does "partial but complete physics" differ from "physics describes extrinsic structure"? Crucial positioning work. Target: research note.
- **Output**: bi-aspectual ontology and dual-aspect traditions

### ✓ 2026-02-20: Write voids article on the framework void
- **Type**: expand-topic
- **Notes**: Suggested by optimistic review 2026-02-20 (afternoon). Research notes complete (voids-framework-void-2026-02-20.md). The framework void argues that our entire conceptual apparatus for understanding consciousness may constitute an invisible cognitive prison. Key elements: three dimensions of framework imprisonment (methodological, semantic, perceptual), the Davidson paradox, the productive tension between McGinn's pessimism and cartographic optimism. Builds on three-kinds-of-void.md, conceptual-impossibility.md, convergent-cognitive-limits.md. See optimistic-2026-02-20-afternoon.md
- **Output**: Write voids article on the framework void

### ✓ 2026-02-20: Fix self-undermining meta-argument in consciousness-and-the-problem-of-theoretical-virtues.md
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Pessimistic review (2026-02-20 afternoon) found the article argues theoretical virtues malfunction for consciousness, then claims this is "predicted by dualism and anomalous for physicalism." This is inconsistent — you cannot argue theory-choice machinery is broken, then use theory-choice reasoning to prefer dualism. Either acknowledge virtue-failure is neutral between dualism and physicalism, or develop the meta-argument more carefully by distinguishing first-order virtue application from second-order reasoning. Also engage with mysterianism as a genuine competitor (cognitive closure offers equally parsimonious reading of virtue failure). See pessimistic-2026-02-20-afternoon.md
- **Output**: obsidian/topics/consciousness-and-the-problem-of-theoretical-virtues.md

### P3: Concept page on the argument from mechanism (sufficiency-necessity non-sequitur)
- **Type**: expand-topic
- **Status**: pending
- **Notes**: Suggested by optimistic-2026-05-08 (High Priority). `topics/out-of-body-experiences.md` lines 83–91 identify and refuse a recurrent inferential pattern in consciousness-debate literature — the move from "phenomenon X can be produced by mechanism M" to "all instances of X are produced by M" — naming it as a non-sequitur ("That a phenomenon can be produced by mechanism M does not show that all instances of the phenomenon are produced by M. Visual experience can be induced by direct cortical stimulation; that does not make ordinary vision hallucinatory"). The pattern is *portable*: it surfaces in psychedelic-experience debates (drug-induced mystical experience produces serotonergic cascade ↛ all mystical experience reduces to serotonergic cascade), in lucid-dreaming debates, in NDE debates, in dissociative-disorder debates, in religious-experience debates, and in many places where dualist-friendly phenomenology has a reductive sufficient-mechanism explanation available. A standalone concept page would (a) name the inferential pattern formally as a *sufficiency-vs-necessity* fallacy in the Map's named-discipline catalogue alongside `concepts/possibility-probability-slippage` and `concepts/evidential-status-discipline`; (b) catalogue the catalogue's existing instances (OBE, lucid dreaming, psychedelics, hypnagogic phenomenology) as worked examples; (c) develop the *symmetric* discipline — the materialist's argument from mechanism is rejected, but so is the dualist's argument from "no mechanism fully explains X therefore mind is involved", which is the parallel non-sequitur in the opposite direction; (d) install the article as a citable handle for dependent articles facing this inference-pattern. The Map already has the discipline operational across multiple articles; what is missing is the *named anchor* for it. Estimated scope: 1500–2000 words. Tenet alignment: methodological — interacts with Tenet 1 (the dualism-friendly inferences depend on the symmetric version of the discipline) and Tenet 5 (Occam's Razor Has Limits — premature parsimony is what the materialist's argument-from-mechanism move attempts). Concepts/ section at ~226/250 capacity — verify cap before placement. See [[reviews/optimistic-2026-05-08]].
- **Source**: optimistic-review (2026-05-08)
- **Generated**: 2026-05-08

### P3: Write concept page — Despite-Commitments / Because-Prediction Boundary-Case Audit (Three-Class Classification)
- **Type**: expand-topic
- **Status**: pending
- **Notes**: Suggested by optimistic-2026-05-16 (Medium Priority). [[topics/introspection-architecture-independence-scoring]] line 102 handles the Gazzaniga split-brain observation as a borderline case (observation despite-commitments with respect to pre-1978 cognitivism; framework because-prediction with respect to its own later predictions). [[pessimistic-2026-05-16]] flagged the lumping of these classes as inflating the headline count. The despite-commitments / because-prediction split is doing a lot of work in the catalogue but its boundary cases are handled inline rather than systematically. A concept page would parse the boundary into three classes: (a) observation-and-framework-both-despite (Nisbett-Wilson 1977 — 1970s cognitivism did not predict the result; the field treated it as anomalous for a decade before absorbing it); (b) observation-despite-but-framework-developed-to-predict (Gazzaniga — the 1978 observation was despite-commitments; the 1985 interpreter framework was constructed to account for it; subsequent confirmations of the framework are because-prediction with respect to the framework itself); (c) observation-and-framework-both-because (Haidt social-intuitionist — moral judgement precedes rational justification was the prior commitment; the experimental confirmation was because-prediction throughout). The classification matters because the catalogue currently lumps (a) and (b) for headline-count purposes and the lumping inflates the count. Page should (a) state the three-class classification cleanly; (b) develop the classification against the present cluster's anchors; (c) audit one or two other clusters' anchors (e.g., the surplus-void's Wallace observation vs Chalmers's framework); (d) state what the three-class classification implies for the licensing-count discipline at the cluster level; (e) cross-link [[common-cause-null]], [[topics/introspection-architecture-independence-scoring]], [[the-surplus-void]], [[apophatic-cartography-four-criteria]]. Section: concepts/ (~226/250). Estimated scope: 2,000 words. Tenet alignment: tightens the [[common-cause-null]] discipline; calibration improvement, not calibration repair. See [[reviews/optimistic-2026-05-16]].
